The prime minister gave a grant to a golf course in his electorate just around the corner from his home, of which he was a member, which he failed to declare. Now we have the health minister, the next wannabe prime minister, doing exactly the same thing.That’s a difficult thing to do. item.title: New York Yankees @ Minnesota Twins: Max Fried vs. Bailey Ober
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: The Yankees are heading to the playoffs. In a season of uncertainty (particularly around injuries), that much is certain after last night’s series-opening comeback victory officially punched their ticket for the ninth time in the last 10 seasons. Everything beyond that, though, is still unknown.While their playoff spot (and likely the top wild card based on the standings) is secure, the team has made it clear that their aspirations are still to win the AL East, which they trail by 3.5 games with 12 to go. Until they get their hands on the Tampa Bay Rays next week in the Bronx, their playoff journey won’t be set in stone, but games like these are important to ensure that what they do that week can directly control their fate.Looking to lock up another series win in Minnesota will be Max Fried, who’s probably hoping to go deeper than his last start against Colorado. He labored through 3.1 innings of work and was removed due to pitch count, but should be pretty close to full-go tonight as he continues to build up. Entering play, he has a 2.73 ERA (155 ERA+) and 2.73 FIP across 99 innings in 18 starts. He did not face the Twins in early July at Yankee Stadium, having been on the injured list with the bone bruise in his elbow.Making the start for Minnesota will be Bailey Ober, who will be toeing the slab for the 23rd time this season. The 31-year-old has been one of their most consistent starters for half a decade now, despite becoming a completely different pitcher as he’s aged. He went from someone who had a very good strikeout rate to one of the lowest among starting pitchers, currently sitting with just 85 strikeouts in 117.2 innings with a 4.28 ERA (98 ERA+). Impressively, he’s only managed to make one career start against the Yankees, allowing three runs in five innings in 2024.Finesse has always been the way he’s gotten batters out, but it’s particularly true as his fastball velocity and, subsequently, usage have cratered over the years, now sitting at just 88.1 mph on average. He has good command and limits hard contact, but has a big issue with allowing barrels due to middling stuff. Against lefties, it’s changeups and four-seamers with a few sliders mixed in, while he throws them much more evenly against righties alongside a sweeper and sinker. : Target Field, Minneapolis, MN: YES, Twins.TV: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), TIBN, The Wolf 102.9 FM, LosTwins.com (MIN): MLB.tv (out-of-market only), Gotham Sports AppFor updates, follow us on , , and , and like us on .

item.title: The Roman telescope has enough gas for 22 years, double NASA's expectations
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is gliding toward its distant observation post on a pinpoint trajectory so precise that engineers estimate the spacecraft's fuel load will last twice as long as their initial expectations, the space agency confirmed Monday.The $4.3 billion observatory's designers originally planned to load enough propellant into Roman's four fuel tanks for a minimum lifetime of five years, plus a potential five-year mission extension. That was a conservative estimate. NASA officials knew an on-target launch and perfect execution of the observatory's first post-launch course correction maneuver would leave Roman with a hearty fuel reserve."As a result of exquisite planning by our orbital dynamics team, brilliant execution by the operations team, and a precise launch from SpaceX, Roman has fuel for at least 22 years of potential science operations," Jamie Dunn, center director at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, said in a press release.

item.title: Iran war cost US $38bn and significantly depleted missile stockpile, report finds

item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: Now, just over two weeks since his surgery, Pogačar was back on the trainer - which presumably means his concussion symptoms have abated."Not quite how we planned to spend September. 😅❤️ At least we have good company. A big thank you to our teams, families, friends and all of you for the amazing support. We are very grateful," he wrote."First time back, collarbone strong, head strong, heart rate high, super happy. Let's go!" a visibly pleased Pogačar says in a video clip in the reel.Pogačar won three stages of the Vuelta and had accumulated a lead of 3:50 over eventual winner Enric Mas (Movistar) before his crash brought his race to an end. He was taken by ambulance to a hospital in Gandia before being transferred to Barcelona.After his surgery, UAE Team Emirates-XRG confirmed that the injuries meant he would not be defending his title at the UCI Road World Championships in Montréal but also announced he had extended his contract through 2032.While he was recovering at home in Monaco, Žigart joined him in ending the season on Saturday after re-fracturing her jaw, originally broken in a horrific crash on stage 2 of the Tour de Suisse in June.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: “Filmmaker” suing PassThePopcorn may be banned user out for revenge

item.content:encoded: Some of the most widely used private torrent trackers for pirating movies suspect that a banned user may have posed as a filmmaker protecting copyrights in a failed attempt to seek revenge.TorrentFreak has been tracking this story closely, reporting last September that an alleged independent filmmaker named Matthew Schneider sued six private trackers for infringing copyrights on some films that he supposedly made. Trackers targeted include PassThePopcorn, BroadcasTheNet, and HDBits. For months, the filmmaker sought to get Cloudflare to unmask operators of the trackers through a copyright fight, which went on until trackers alerted the court last month that Schneider appeared to be an impostor.In a sworn declaration, the actual filmmaker behind the movies cited in the complaint wrote that he had no association to the plaintiff in the case. “I am not involved in, nor have I ever appeared in, this case,” Schneider wrote.

item.title: MLB Mid-September Check-in: NL West
item.author: Estevão Maximo
item.content:encoded: Every day, Pinstripe Alley offers updates on what the Yankees’ top American League opponents are up to through the . The AL East is well-trodden ground there, but with the final month of the season just ahead, we’re going to take a peek around MLB as a whole and check in with each of the other five divisions. Who’s surprising? Who’s underwhelming? Who’s simply mediocre at the moment? Read on and find out.First Place: Los Angeles Dodgers (90-59) Max Muncy (4.2 fWAR) Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.3 fWAR)Perhaps even more clearly than last season, there is a bit of a disconnect between the expectation of how the Dodgers will look come playoff time and their actual record — the latter has been on par with the other two division leaders in the National League for most of the season, not quite lapping the league like the former has been since the offseason. It should be noted that the Dodgers have managed to build a little cushion over Atlanta as of late though, entering the week with a three-game lead in the loss column. It’s understandable how we got here, especially after they made up for the absence of starting pitcher Shohei Ohtani in the playoffs with the addition of Tarik Skubal at the deadline.Speaking of baseball’s unicorn, the biggest development recently over in Chavez Ravine has been the IL placement of Ohtani with right-biceps inflammation, one of many issues bothering Ohtani for quite a while now. Considering he has already resumed baseball activities, expectations are that he should be back in the lineup come the end of the regular season. The main question is how much these nagging issues will affect Ohtani’s ability to hit in the playoffs — a hobbled-up Ohtani, below his recent standard, still managed to hit 30 homers and accumulate a 142 wRC+ this regular season, both good enough to lead this potent lineup.Ohtani isn’t the only high-profile hitter currently missing from the Dodgers lineup; they are also without Andy Pages, absent with a fractured hand. That being said, the reigning back-to-back champs are also confident about the return of Pages come playoff time, which would technically leave this lineup at full strength — actual full strength depends on Kyle Tucker’s recent hot stretch carrying over after an incredibly underwhelming first year with the Dodgers. Moving over to the pitching side, the rotation that already dominated last year’s postseason gets the boost of Skubal — once again with both Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell fresh off campaigns in which they seldom pitched in the regular season, combining for just 18 starts.San Diego Padre Fernando Tatis Jr. (4.8 fWAR) Mason Miller (3.5 fWAR)Potentially the hottest team in the National League right now, the San Diego Padres, as the Yankees recently learned on a trip to Petco Park, possess quite the dangerous team. Since that series with New York, all the Padres have done is win, taking advantage of a soft part of the schedule by sweeping the Nationals and Giants. The NL is so strong that even with this productive run, San Diego is only three games up on Arizona in the loss column for the final Wild Card spot — these two teams are set to play on the final weekend of the season.The Padres have flourished with the improved form of Fernando Tatis Jr., possessing a 25-14 record since the start of August. Running a lot more than your average team, in large part thanks to the aggressiveness of Tatis — who leads the league having been caught stealing 13 times — the Padres have the rare distinction of possessing three different players with at least 20 stolen bases. Tatis is joined by Jackson Merrill and Xander Bogaerts to make up that dangerous trio on the basepaths.A key boost to the Padres’ playoff chances comes in the recent return of Nick Pivetta. Just a season ago, Pivetta was outperforming former Yankee Michael King and current AL Cy Young candidate Dylan Cease to be the ace of this staff. It’s a position he more or less slots right back into, although it should be noted that King has kicked things up a notch — and even more importantly, the former Yankee has been healthy the whole year. Overall, this is a sneaky, quality team, and it wouldn’t be a surprise seeing them give any NL division winner a run for their money if they can hold off Arizona.Third Place: Arizona Diamondbacks (79-71, 11.5 GB) Gabriel Moreno (4.4 fWAR) Eduardo Rodríguez (3.2 fWAR)Guess how many baseball teams currently have not one, not two, but three separate players with an fWAR of 4.0 or higher. That distinction belongs to the Chicago Cubs and the Arizona Diamondbacks. Interestingly, in the middle of the Diamondbacks trio, you won’t find the player who you could argue is Arizona’s most talented hitter, Ketel Marte. After an unexplained absence during a series against the Red Sox that led to him being placed on the Restricted List, Marte has returned to action — while his numbers in September aren’t anything special, his availability dramatically affects the makeup of this lineup.If you’re wondering how the Diamondbacks got here with a subpar performance from a star hitter and their highest-paid player, Corbin Burnes, basically missing the whole year, it’s been a mix of breakout performances and bounce-back campaigns. Moreno, who had already established himself as a reliable catcher, is producing career-high hitting stats across the board, while Eduardo Rodríguez is having the greatest season of his career by a wide margin in year No. 11 as a big leaguer.Circling back to Burnes, the former Cy Young winner made his return to the big leagues recently, still on a tight leash. The potential to get Burnes and Marte producing at a high level in the playoffs could make this Arizona team a dangerous one. However, before even thinking about that, they have to run down the Padres, an ungrateful task given how San Diego is playing.Fourth Place: San Francisco Giants (62-88) Rafael Devers (3.4 fWAR)* Logan Webb (3.1 fWAR)*Technically, Luis Arraez is still in the number one spot at 3.8, but he was traded to the Phillies at the deadline.After years of unsuccessfully trying to lure a superstar to the Bay Area, the Giants found their man in Rafael Devers. Leaving aside the positive impact of this move for the Yankees, particularly given what Boston took to get rid of him, one player alone has a very limited impact on the fate of a team.Sure, there are many specific flaws we could point to as to why this team is so close to the bottom, but there are too many to go through them all. Ultimately, it’d be shortsighted to focus on the down year from Logan Webb, for instance, or other specific letdowns for a team whose process seems to be in question.No matter how you look at it, the reviews around Tony Vitello’s first year as a manager in the big leagues are far from flattering. To call bringing in a skipper without any big-league experience a risky move is an understatement. It’s fair to say that the Buster Posey regime is already under heavy scrutiny.Last Place: Colorado Rockies (55-94) Jake McCarthy (2.8 fWAR) Kyle Freeland (1.1 fWAR)Something that Mike Tomlin said on a broadcast during Week 1 of the NFL season, quoting a former player, noting that “the Browns is the Browns,” stuck in the back of my mind. That could easily apply to the Colorado Rockies in Major League Baseball, a franchise that has been at the bottom of the barrel for too long to be genuinely optimistic about a rebuild project — at least before seeing promising signs to back that up.It’s 2026, and Kyle Freeland is still showing up as their most productive pitcher. The injury to Chase Dollander, who has been a rare, exciting young arm to take the mound at Coors Field, certainly hurt this team’s outlook in 2026. But their primary problems remain the same, and a solution doesn’t seem to be on the horizon.

item.title: 18-year-old dies of measles in PA from severe neurological complication
item.author: Beth Mole
item.content:encoded: According to the Mifflin County coroner, Andrea L. Alcalde, the 18-year-old's cause of death was determined to be acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), which is a rare but known severe complication of measles. The condition is characterized by a rapidly progressing autoimmune disorder in which aberrant inflammation from an infection strips away the protective coverings of nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord. Before measles vaccines were widely used, ADEM was commonly associated with measles, though other viral infections can also spur its development.

Sunrise in Brownsville, Texas, is 7:17 am CT, so the launch could make for some striking imagery.The super heavy lift rocket will be carrying 26 of the larger V3 Starlink satellites into an orbit 275 km above the Earth. In an update on its website, SpaceX said the Starship upper stage will seek to complete six orbits around the Earth before completing its mission after about 10 hours.

item.title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
item.author: Jeremy Hsu
item.content:encoded: Agility Robotics has debuted its first humanoid robot engineered to work safely near humans without risking harm to flesh-and-blood coworkers. Such safety features could unlock many more opportunities to use such robots inside warehouses and automotive factories—all without requiring isolated robot work cells and physical separation barriers.When Agility’s new Digit 5 robot detects a person at a distance, it can autonomously take precautions, like moving to avoid the person or standing still so the person can pass by without getting closer. If a person is getting into close proximity with Digit 5, the robot can even choose to squat and assume a seated position.“The robot was designed with a complex safe motion system that can take a variety of different mitigations depending on exactly what sort of human presence is detected,” Pras Velagapudi, chief technology officer at Agility, told Ars.

item.title: MLB Mid-September Check-in: NL Central
item.author: Matt Ferenchick
item.content:encoded: Every day, Pinstripe Alley offers updates on what the Yankees’ top American League opponents are up to through the . The AL East is well-trodden ground there, but with the Trade Deadline behind us, we’re going to take a peek around MLB as a whole and check in with each of the other five divisions. Who’s surprising? Who’s underwhelming? Who’s simply mediocre at the moment? Read on and find out.We’ve reached the halfway point of September, several teams have now clinched postseason spots, and several more will soon. With just a couple weeks of regular season baseball left, let’s check in on the NL Central.Note: Records and stats are through games played on September 13th.First Place: Milwaukee Brewers (93-57) Brice Turang (5.2 fWAR) Jacob Misiorowski (6.0 fWAR)The Brewers won the race to be the first team to clinch a playoff spot over the weekend, and they’re now closing in on the NL Central title. They’re in a good position to finish with the best record in all of baseball as well.They have an obvious absolute star in Misiorowski, but the most remarkable thing about the Brewers is that they’re just generally solid at almost every spot. Only one of their hitters with over 400 plate appearances has a wRC+ below the 100 average, and that’s Christian Yelich, who’s still in the 90s. You could’ve said similar things about last year’s Brewers, and they ended up getting shoved aside by the Dodgers in the NLCS, so we shall see.Second Place: Chicago Cubs (83-67, 10 GB) Pete Crow-Armstrong (9.8 fWAR) Ben Brown (2.0 fWAR)Going into Monday, the Cubs would have the third best record were they an AL team. Instead in the NL Central, they’re way off the pace of the division lead. As of now, the Cubs are safely in the NL playoffs, but not so safe that they can rest on their laurels. They lost five of their last seven games going into Monday, so they can’t afford to let that skid continue.As a team, the Cubs are incredibly reliant on their hitting and defense, while pitching has been a massive struggle for them. The two facets of the team are on such opposite poles that they’re going to go down as one of the most unbalanced teams of all time. They have the possible NL MVP in Crow-Armstrong, but can he and the rest of the lineup overcome that pitching? It’ll be fascinating to see play out.Third Place: Pittsburgh Pirates (75-75, 18 GB) Brandon Lowe (4.1 fWAR) Paul Skenes (4.8 fWAR)It was wild to realize when putting together this post that the Pirates are basically in need of a miracle run to get into the playoffs in the NL, but they would be a game out of contention with that record in the AL.It’s probably too late for Pittsburgh to rally and make the playoffs, but there are some things they can take away from this season. They’ve gotten some good seasons out of some of their young, up and coming players. One of those players is Skenes, who has only been merely “good” instead of “Cy Young Award great.” It’s somewhat worrying that he’s taken a step back, but if the Pirates figure that out, they could be a team that is intriguing next year.Fourth Place: St. Louis Cardinals (74-76, 19 GB) JJ Weatherholt (4.4 fWAR) Andre Pallante and Kyle Leahy (2.6 fWAR)You can copy and paste some of what was said above about the Pirates and apply that to the Cardinals. Seven different St. Louis hitters aged 27 or younger have put up above average OPS+es on the season. Pallante and Michael McGreevy are both younger pitchers who’ve had pretty good years. They’re also gone nowhere in the standings, really.Fifth Place: Cincinnati Reds (70-79, 22.5 GB) Elly De La Cruz (5.7 fWAR) Chase Burns (4.4 fWAR)The good news for the Reds is that Burns looks like a possible stud worthy of the No. 2 overall pick that he was in 24. More good news is that De La Cruz remains an absolute freak of nature and a genuine star. Not a ton else has gone right for Cincinnati, though. Their 22.5-game deficit in the division is the most of anyone in the league besides the Rockies and Giants in the NL West, both of whom are very bad.

item.title: As the politicians play catchup the tech bros agree: we may only have a decade left | John Crace
item.author: John Crace
item.content:encoded: US president insists that fears expressed by top experts are a hoax – and that humanity can sleep easy while he’s at the wheelWe can all sleep easy. In a post on his Truth Social account, Donald Trump has declared that fears over artificial intelligence were all a hoax dreamed up by conspiracy theorists. Obviously that includes the top bods at Anthropic and its competitors, who all called for a coordinated global slowdown while the industry works out how to mitigate the risks. Still, good to know the tech bros are just fantasists and space cadets at heart.All that was needed to keep humanity safe and well, The Donald insisted, was a president with a very high IQ. Someone very like him. The only man alive who could out-think the combined power of the world’s supercomputers. He could tell them where to draw the line and they would reprogram themselves to back off. Inside every AI network is a default off switch that kneels before the US president. Trump can rewire the world with the power of his mind.Continue reading...

item.title: The Guardian view on the Bank of England’s £120bn bill: power without accountability | Editorial
item.author: Editorial
item.content:encoded: Quantitative tightening has blurred the line between monetary and fiscal policy, leaving ministers accountable for decisions they cannot directly controlWhen Labour made the Bank of England independent in 1997, the idea was that the Bank set interest rates while the Treasury taxed and spent. Monetary policy was in Threadneedle Street, fiscal policy in Whitehall. But in August the Bank of England quietly slipped out that its key policy could cost the Treasury £120bn. That policy – quantitative tightening (QT) – clearly ought to be rethought and the policy of the Treasury indemnifying the Bank for its losses ended. Last year, ministers paid the Bank £17bn to cover these arguably notional losses – an amount considerably larger than the budget of the Ministry of Justice, which is dealing with a real prisons crisis.Bank independence was constructed for a world in which monetary policy decisions had predictable and indirect fiscal effects. The financial crisis, Covid, war and fractious trade disputes have contributed to ending that world. The Bank bought up government bonds to support the economy via its quantitative easing (QE) programme. But the constitutional settlement – of an independent central bank working out on its own what to do with those bonds – has not caught up. The game is surely up when a former Bank deputy governor, Charlie Bean, acknowledges that independence cannot justify effectively giving power to an unelected monetary policy committee (MPC) over decisions with great consequences for public spending.Continue reading...

item.title: Demand for EV chargers is outstripping supply, says ChargePoint report
item.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
item.content:encoded: There might not be the same degree of optimism regarding electric vehicle adoption as a few short years ago, but the transition toward battery-electric vehicles continues nevertheless. More than 1.8 million EVs had already been sold between the start of this year and the end of August, according to analysts. And in the US, there has been a large uptick in drivers considering EVs that they might have written off last year, due to escalating fuel prices with no clear end in sight. Despite this, charging infrastructure continues to lag, according to a new report from ChargePoint.“All in all, things are moving forward. I think the North American market has been better shaped than a lot of the press reports,” said ChargePoint CEO Rick Wilmer. “Part of it is just the data we see in terms of the amount of RFPs that we receive for charging solutions. They haven't slowed down. We reported quarter over quarter growth in the last quarter we reported. And you look at the data around used EVs going up in price because the demand is so high. I saw a recent report… EV retention rates are 96 percent. So those folks that are putting their leased cars on the used market, they're not going back to gas, they're going to another EV,” he said.Beyond that, cheap electric trucks from Slate and Ford indicate further future demand for charging. “When you look at how much interest there is in the used EVs that are at parity with an equivalent gas vehicle, that tells you the appetite is there for EVs if it's the right vehicle at the right price point," Wilmer said. "So I think the auto OEMs, maybe not homogeneously, but they're figuring out what the market wants in North America, and they're starting to introduce those vehicles, which I don't think a lot of the forward-looking forecasts accommodate the fact that the product market fit is getting better coming out of the car companies.”

item.title: MLB Mid-September Check-in: NL East
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: Every day, Pinstripe Alley offers updates on what the ’ top American League opponents are up to through the . The AL East is well-trodden ground there, but with the season’s final month halfway over, we’re going to take a peek around MLB as a whole and check in with each of the other five divisions. Who’s surprising? Who’s underwhelming? Who’s simply mediocre at the moment? Read on and find out.(Note: Records and standings are up to date through games played on Sunday, September 13th.)First Place: Atlanta Braves (88-62)Michael Harris II (4.0 fWAR)Chris Sale (5.7 fWAR)Believe it or not, the Atlanta Braves have had a below-average offense statistically so far in 2026, despite boasting elite names like Ronald Acuña Jr., Matt Olson, Michael Harris II, and Drake Baldwin. They rank 19th in wRC+ with a 98 mark.The pitching has done the heavy lifting despite dealing with lots of injuries from the start. Right now, talented hurlers like Spencer Schwellenbach, Spencer Strider, Bryce Elder, and Robert Suárez are on the injured list, yet the team is fourth in MLB with a 3.59 ERA.With a 3.41 ERA, the Braves’ bullpen is the best in the National League. It’s led by closer Raisel Iglesias (2.78 ERA), Didier Fuentes (2.27 ERA, 31.5 K%), Dylan Lee (3.09 ERA), and other unheralded heroes like Dylan Dodd, Víctor Mederos, Ray Kerr, and Brent Suter. The addition of Tyler Mahle (1.25 ERA in seven starts as a Brave) at the deadline was just what the doctor ordered, and Chris Sale (2.18 ERA) has been as good as ever.Harris’ all-around game sets the tone, and Acuña’s power-speed prowess (17 HR, 20 SB in 97 G) elevates the team’s ceiling. Having Matt Olson picking up the power pace with 39 homers after two straight campaigns with 29 also helps, of course. The Braves, as their record indicates, are very hard to beat. Suárez returning from injury soon could make them even tougher.Second Place: Philadelphia Phillies (83-67)Bryce Harper (3.5 fWAR)Christopher Sánchez (5.8 fWAR)Bryce Harper refuses to decline and is sporting a cool 140 wRC+ with 28 home runs this year. He and Kyle Schwarber, who has 44 homers and owns a 132 wRC+, are virtually the Phillies’ offense, though: the unit has put up the fourth-worst wRC+ in baseball with a 92 mark. Trea Turner (83 wRC+) has had a rough season, and the same can be said about JT Realmuto (78 wRC+), Alec Bohm (89 wRC+), Luis Arraez (80 wRC+), and Justin Crawford (82 wRC+). Runs are hard to come by in Philadelphia.Christopher Sánchez (2.79 ERA), Jesús Luzardo (2.87 ERA), and Zack Wheeler (3.14 ERA) are a formidable rotation trio, but Aaron Nola has been inconsistent, and there are now questions about the health of Luzardo’s shoulder.Despite solid seasons from Jhoan Durán, Tim Mayza, and Jonathan Bowlan, the bullpen is more ‘meh’ than ‘great’. This team will go as far as the rotation takes it, although a rebound from some of their struggling hitters would certainly help matters. The Phillies are fighting with the Chicago Cubs for the top Wild Card spot in the senior circuit. Unless the offense improves, however, it’s hard to see them making much noise in October.Third Place: Miami Marlins (74-76)Otto López (5.4 fWAR)Sandy Alcántara (3.1 fWAR)The Marlins are 7.5 games behind the final Wild Card spot, so they aren’t really contending. After their disastrous 2024 and decent 2025, however, 2026 has been about finding potentially useful long-term pieces. And they have had some success.As expected, Otto López’s stats have considerably diminished in the second half (79 wRC+, 1 HR, 13 SB) after a really strong performance before the break (137 wRC+, 9 HR, 17 SB). Still, a 10-homer, 30-steal season with a 116 wRC+ and 5.4 fWAR is nothing to sneeze at.The Marlins’ offense, a perfectly average unit that ranks 14th in baseball, has some interesting hitters. With the exception of Joe Mack and Jakob Marsee, every starter boasts an above-average wRC+: Javier Sanoja, Xavier Edwards, Heriberto Hernández, Griffin Conine, Kyle Stowers, Esteury Ruiz, and López.Before going down with a neck strain in July, Max Meyer (2.68 ERA in 20 starts) showed enough to be considered a frontline guy and a building block. Alcántara has been steady, and Eury Pérez had a huge summer before hitting a wall in September.Overall, the Marlins have a solid core and a top-ten farm that includes injured pitching prospects Thomas White and Robby Snelling. If they play their cards right, they might make some noise next year.Fourth Place: Washington Nationals (70-81)James Wood (4.1 fWAR)Cade Cavalli (3.6 fWAR)Speaking of making noise, the Nationals’ offense can certainly score some runs. The group is fifth in MLB and fourth in the National League with a 104 wRC+, and ranks fourth in homers with 198. Of course, having James Wood (30 HR, 21 SB, 147 wRC+) and CJ Abrams (30 HR, 29 SB, 125 wRC+) certainly helps matters. These two will be a problem for MLB pitching staffs for a long time.Dylan Crews’ development has stalled, and they don’t have Curtis Mead and Luis García Jr. anymore, but there’s a lot of talent in Washington’s offense besides the two aforementioned stars. Daylen Lile (20 HR, 15 SB) and Keibert Ruiz (113 wRC+) have had solid offensive seasons, and Brady House has potential. Former Yankees prospect Andrés Chaparro has been excellent against both lefties and righties.Pitching, however, is a problem. Washington has the worst staff in the National League and the second-worst in the majors with a 5.14 ERA. Cade Cavalli (3.12 ERA) has had a breakout campaign, and Andrew Álvarez has been solid. There’s not much else beyond that, although adding the injured Connelly Early was a nice coup. The Nationals, with a solid core and a top-ten farm, are at the very least interesting again.Fifth Place: New York Mets (69-80)Carson Benge (3.3 fWAR)Nolan McLean (3.1 fWAR)The season in Queens has been a disaster, but it at least gave them a strong platform to develop Carson Benge and he’s looking like a budding star. The rookie outfielder is slashing a cool .271/.334/.411 with a 109 wRC+, 17 home runs and 22 steals after a brutal start. Juan Soto has survived two injured list stints to post a 147 wRC+ and 25 round-trippers, and Francisco Lindor reached 20 dingers with a solid 111 after having to deal with hamate bone surgery.A.J. Ewing emerged as another potential building block in the outfield, although it remains to be seen if he’s a starter or more of a fourth outfielder. Brett Baty, who was brutal for most of the first half, is closing the season strong with a 125 wRC+ after the break and a 236 mark in September so far.Despite trading away Clay Holmes, Freddy Peralta, and lots of relievers at the deadline, the Mets have a top-ten ERA in the second half, at 3.38. Zach Thornton and Nate Lavender have been amazing stories in the rotation and bullpen, respectively, and Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are excellent building blocks.With a few interesting young pieces, two superstars, and lots of money to spend, the Mets could be dangerous in 2027, if there’s baseball. The 2026 campaign, however, was a huge disappointment.

item.title: 'Our tactics will change a lot' - Absence of Tadej Pogačar leave Slovenia casting around for other options in Road World Championships
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: When it comes to the absence of double rainbow jersey Tadej Pogačar in the upcoming Road World Championships, almost every major squad has accepted that the race takes on a very different format and they will have to adapt accordingly. But the nation for whom Pogačar's non-participation will change things the most is surely his own home country and the riders who usually back him there."Our tactics will change a lot," Domen Novak, Pogačar's teammate at UAE Team Emirates-XRG, , to the point where Novak himself, a participant in every World's since 2020 and a DNF in all of them, will not be going.Regularly the powerhouse rider for the first part of the course for Slovenia before dropping out after his work in the first 150 to 200 kilometres are done, this time round "I'm not going to the Worlds because I'm going to the Tour of Croatia [CRO Race - September 22-27] and it's a big change," Novak told during the Vuelta a España, where he was one of just four UAE riders who completed the stage race."For us, it changes a lot, especially for me, what would I do there? We don't have leaders, so it's not like we need to pull all day."Without Tadej, I wouldn't have the same job anyway and it's going to be difficult to get in the breaks. I don't think they'd let us do that much. So I'm going to Croatia."Whilst Primoz Roglič was an unexpected addition to the Slovenia lineup when the Vuelta was announced, Novak feels that the best options for his teammates like the veteran Red Bull racer, as well as Matej Mohorič, Jakob Omrzel and Jan Tratnik, will be trying to get in the moves "when the guys start getting dropped", after the early skirmishes have settled down."We should wait all day and then start looking for chances," the 31-year-old Novak argues.As for who could be up there, Roglič himself has not been willing to express his plans too clearly. With his best result a sixth place in 2020 - before Pogačar logically began dominating the Slovenian team plans - Roglič also took 11th in 2025. He's always shone on hilly Classics circuits, so he could have options."I decided to do the Worlds now there is some race intensity in my legs, but we have no expectations," Roglič said after the Vuelta."I just want to go there, enjoy it and do my best, and the race will tell me what place I should be.""He's growing year by year, he also won some races in the past like [Junior] Paris-Roubaix and the Giro Next Gen. He's a guy to watch," Novak said about Omrzel, a former teammate of his at the Slovanian Adria Mobil squad and an occasional Vuelta training partner, too, as they are neighbours."He races very smart when he gets in breakaways, here in the Vuelta he got in two and pulled back a lot of time overall as well as getting the win. And winning a first stage in a first Grand Tour is pretty exceptional."However, when it comes to examples of how to race the Worlds without Pogačar, Slovenia are also harking back to times when riders like Jan Tratnik attempted to pull off last-minute heists at the 2023 road race, breaking away late in an attempt to snaffle the bronze. Part of the move that set up Pogačar on the road to his first rainbow jersey in Zurich, Tratnik will also be back again in Canada, but this time fighting for his own chances."Tratnik can be good, he was nearly third in Australia but they caught him 50 metres from the finish," Novak said. "So now he can go for more. In any case, I wish the guys in Canada all the best."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'Hard things suck because they're hard' - Lachlan Morton helps Adventure For All teammate through 10-hour ride at Rebecca's Private Idaho
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Rebecca's Private Idaho in southern Idaho, the three-day event featuring 203 miles across 12,645 feet of elevation gain, was all about the queen stage on Sunday, September 13. On the final day, the standalone 'Fully Loaded Baked Potato' race, with 118 miles and nearly half of the elevation gain, all ears were on event founder Rebecca Rusch for an update on the event, while all eyes were on a new teammate for former WorldTour rider and gravel pioneer Lachlan Morton (EF Education-EasyPost). Morton completed the course as a rider-coach for the Adventure For All non-profit, helping 20-year-old Christian Loafman finish in 10:54:03. This RPI event was not about winning or the four-hour deficit to men's stage winner Allan Schroeder, or the three-hour deficit to women's winner Britt Mason. It was about completing a challenge. Loafman, a neurodivergent endurance athlete who has faced significant medical challenges since the age of two, now adds this high-elevation gravel stage race to his list of accomplishments, having completed Unbound Gravel 100 in May with Ian Boswell (Wahoo-Specialized-RCC). "He was really determined. I was never questioning whether he could get it done. I recognised pretty early on we got a pretty similar mindset, and he committed to it. He was hurting, I've been in that place so I know what that feels like," Morton said about his ride partner."The roads are rough, high elevation, the course is always throwing something at you, and then we had a big headwind coming home. So plenty of challenges out there today. "We had a definite low point on the new loop, on the far end. The headwind was like ripping off the mountain. I could see the body language, he was quiet. So I said we're gonna stop here, take the pack off, sit down, stretch for a sec, eat something and just do a total reset. "It was wild, he really reset and then took off. From then I'm like we're gonna make it. He was in that [hurt] locker deep for probably six hours. It's not something most people can tolerate. Hard things suck because they're hard."Rusch steps away from RPIIn 2027, Rusch, a seven-time world champion and celebrated endurance athlete, will step away from the event, which will be rebranded as The Big Lost, taking its name from a 'disappearing' river, the Big Lost River, that moved underground in the area."14 years ago, there wasn’t even a gravel culture. There wasn’t the equipment, the community, or the trails I now call home. I was the only one riding up Trail Creek. This weekend, we closed the final chapter of Rebecca’s Private Idaho, and I was overcome. Not with sadness, but with pride, for what we built together."So yes, this is the last RPI. But it’s a chapter, not the end of the book. The race lives on as The Big Lost, under new leadership, on the same trails you love," Rusch posted on social media, saying she would now focus on coaching and her podcast, What's the Rusch.Former two-time U23 Canadian national champion Sidney McGill and 19-year-old rising Canadian talent Rhett Bates won the elite C2 races on Saturday at Canmore Cross in Alberta, the North American opener for the 2026-2027 cyclocross season.McGill dominated the women's field in a time of 53:30, with USA's Amelia Shea finishing second, a little more than three minutes back, and Christiane Bilodeau another minute later for third. Bates needed a strong kick at the end to distance USA's Ben Frederick, who was seven seconds off the winning time of 1:00:33. First-year U23 US rider Jack Billowitz completed the podium, holding off Mark Fagnan of Canada.The upcoming weekend features the start of six UCI races that comprise the USCX series, one C1 and one C2 at each of the trio of events beginning with Rochester Cyclocross on September 19-20. Virginia's Blue Ridge GO Cross follows on September 26-27 and the series concludes with Charm City Cross on October 3-4.Marles Mejías (Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY28) and Cade Bickmore (Team Cadence Cyclery pb Waldo Racing) won elite titles at Bucks County Classic in Doylestown, Pennsylvania on Sunday. Now in its 22nd edition, the Bucks County Classic marks the traditional conclusion for criterium racing in the US. Early rain left the 1.4-mile, eight-corner course slippery for the Penn Medicine Doylestown Health Pro Women race, which saw a large crash on lap three split the field. From there, most of the favourites rode in a 16-rider front group which contested a final-lap sprint.Last year's runner-up and 2024 winner Mejías took the lead on the final uphill straightaway and saw only daylight for the victory. 2023 winner Skylar Schneider (L39ION of Los Angeles) could not get around the Cuban rider and settled for second. WorldTour rider Barbara Guarischi (SD Worx-ProTime) swept past Arrielle Verhaaren (Automatic Racing) to grab the final podium spot.“I love this race and I decided at the last minute to go, and I’m so happy I did,” said Marlies, who was joined by her family. “The race was really hard and the group got smaller, but I felt strong. I love an uphill power sprint, so when we came into the finish I knew I had a good chance. It was a really special win.”It was a different scenario for the Thompson Pro Men’s race, with a group of five riders lapping the field with 11 circuits to go. Bickmore, Michael Reidenbach (Total Civil Construction), Daniel Uhranowsky (Visit Pittsburgh) and Kelly Benefits Cycling duo Julien Ruhe and Dillon Lee were all able to reconnect with other teammates to position for the charge to the line.Using pulls on the final two laps from Sam Smith and Danny Summerhill, Bickmore edged Ruhe for the victory. Dillon then gave Kelly Benefits two riders on the podium with Lee riding solo for third. Reidenbach was fourth and Uhranowsky fifth.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'Time to look somewhere else' – Boundary-pushing Dutch rider Jan-Willem van Schip is done with cycling
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Jan-Willem van Schip has announced his retirement from racing. The Dutch rider, a former two-time track world champion, called time on his career in a short Instagram post on Sunday."Time to look somewhere else," Van Schip wrote. "I'm going to stop cycling. Come and see me at my farewell during [the Rotterdam Six Day]."The 32-year-old rider had raced for several teams on the road and track during his 13-year career, including A BLOC, Parkhotel Valkenburg, BEAT Cycling Club, and Roompot.His biggest successes came on the track, with World Championships wins in the Points Race in 2019 and the Madison in 2023. He also won the European Madison title in 2021 and has several UCI World Cup wins and national track titles to his name.Van Schip took three wins on the road, too, including the 2017 Ronde van Drenthe and a stage of the 2019 Baloise Belgium Tour.He has been perhaps best known for his bike positioning and aerodynamic innovations, which pushed the boundaries of the UCI rulebook several times over the years.Van Schip has racked up a host of disqualifications over the years, with his bike set-ups often falling foul of the sport's rules.In 2021, 2023, and 2025, Van Schip was disqualified from races for using illegal handlebar setups, while earlier this year he was disqualified from the Tour of Hellas for using an illegal riding position.His most recent infraction came at the Ronde de L'Oise after he was caught racing with a bidon down the front of his jersey in contravention of UCI regulation 2.12.007 3.2 – 'Use of non-compliant clothing, helmet or any other item or accessory worn by the rider'."For us, the situation is becoming a bit untenable," he said."We are just a small Continental team, you know. We are absolutely not Visma or whatever. Everywhere Jan-Willem races, it almost always costs us 1,000 Swiss Francs in fines. As a team, that is unsustainable."Van Schip said earlier this year that "I don't really feel welcome in cycling." Now, he's calling an end to his career, with his last outing on the road coming at the Dutch National Championships in June.His final race will come at the Rotterdam Six Day track event, which runs from December 1-6.

item.author: Gloria Dickie

item.title: Ferrari not yet switching focus to 2027 F1 car
The sinister influence of crypto billionaires on our politics | Letters
item.author: Guardian Staff
item.content:encoded: Readers respond to the news that Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching a donation from Ben DeloCryptocurrency is often sold as decentralised and democratic, yet its real behaviour resembles gravity: wealth is pulled inexorably into a few vast centres while draining from everyone else (Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo, 12 September). Early adopters, insiders and whales acquire huge holdings at negligible cost. Their size then shapes the market, drawing in ordinary investors whose money ultimately fuels those already at the top.Because crypto generates no cash flow and produces little real economic output, it becomes structurally zero‑sum. One person’s gain is another’s loss, and the system relies on a continual inflow of participants whose contributions sustain the fortunes of a minority.Continue reading...

item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Slow Joe Doyle
item.author: Jonathan Farrar
item.content:encoded: Before he was known as Slow Joe, Judd Bruce Doyle was a right-handed pitcher growing up in the middle of Kansas. Like most of the time, his love of baseball was not born in an organized league, but in the school lot and in local games in his community featuring players of all ages. September 15, 1881 (Clay Center, KS) November 21, 1947 (Tannersville, NY) 1906-1910Born before the turn of the century, Doyle was small even by the standards of the time. He was reported by most accounts at 5-foot-8 and 150 pounds. However, growing up working on the family farm made Doyle what many call country strong or stout. Despite having some strength behind his small frame, Doyle relied on changing pace and his arm slots to keep hitters off balance, much like former Yankee folk hero Nestor Cortes. Doyle and his mix of overhand and submarine deliveries tossed a drop ball, rise ball, changeup, and the legendary spitball.Doyle’s professional baseball journey started right after he graduated from Clay Center High School in 1901. This kicked off a five-year run through the amateur ranks. In 1902, Doyle suited up for the Fort Worth Panthers and the New Orleans Pelicans. Then, in 1903, Doyle joined the Baton Rouge Red Sticks in the Cotton States League. In his first season in Baton Rouge, Doyle went 16-9 and helped the team win the league championship. He started the 1904 season back in a Red Sticks jersey, but would finish that season and play the 1905 season for the Wheeling Stogies.After playing well for the Stogies, Doyle finally landed the coveted contract with a professional team when his rights were sold to the New York Highlanders in August of 1905. Slow Joe burst onto the scene a few days later, making his debut on August 25, 1906. In his first start, Doyle threw a six-hit shutout against the Cleveland Naps. He followed that up with another shutout against the Washington Senators in his second game. The rookie appeared in nine games total, tossing 45.1 innings with a 2-1 record and 2.38 ERA.Following the hot start to his career, Doyle came into the 1907 season expecting to be a big part of the Highlanders rotation. Doyle appeared in 29 games, making 23 starts. This led to what would stand as his career-high 193.2 innings with an impressive 2.65 ERA and an 11-11 record. Doyle led the Highlanders with 15 complete games and 94 strikeouts. It was also during this run that his reputation for slow playing really took hold. The Washington Times referred to Doyle as the Human Snail due to his long stretches between pitches.In 1908, Doyle’s third season, Slow Joe was officially the name adopted and used by the press as an unofficial, official name. Doyle’s arm did not handle the large workload from the year before well, and he was limited to 12 games, only four starts, and only 48 innings. Despite being effective when he pitched, the lack of availability started to be the story.Doyle asked for extra days of rest between starts in 1909, and it led to a rebound. He pitched in 17 games, making 15 starts, tossing 125.2 innings, and going 8-6 on the year. Still just 27 years old, Doyle’s arm simply could not handle the workload of a normal pitcher of the time.The Highlanders had Doyle on their roster to start the 1910 season but ended up cutting him halfway through the year. The Cincinnati Reds signed Doyle, and he pitched the final part of the season for them. After making five relief appearances for the Reds, Doyle’s major league career was over at just 28 years old after the 1910 season.Beyond his memorable nickname, Slow Joe Doyle holds a legendary status among modern sports collectors due to one of the rarest and most valuable printing blunders in baseball history: the 1910 T206 “Slow Joe” Doyle error card. During the production of the iconic tobacco card set, the American Lithographic Company accidentally designated Doyle as playing for “Nat’l” rather than “Amer” in his New York uniform. After catching the mistake, the printers pulled the printing plate, scrapped off the “Nat’l” letters, slapped the plate back into the machine, and continued printing. Today, fewer than a dozen authentic copies are known to exist, making it more rare than the famed Honus Wagner T206 card.Happy birthday, Slow Joe!

item.title: 'Perfection doesn't exist' – Can Wout van Aert maintain top form after admitting Vuelta wasn't just a 'preparation race' for World Championships?
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: It will be his first appearance at the road Worlds since Glasgow 2023, where he finished second behind eternal rival Mathieu van der Poel, and he's approaching the showpiece event in some of the best form of his career after the Vuelta a España. "Perfection doesn't exist. I think in two weeks it's already there; [I] definitely have good legs and big goals, so we need to try and recover from this Vuelta and we go for it in Montreal," said Van Aert after the Vuelta's finale in Granada. "This wasn't a preparation race, you know. This was a goal in itself, from which we tried to get the most out of every day. The World Championships are coming up, but so far we have naturally focused on the Vuelta."Belgium's other superstar rider, Evenepoel, has been racing in Canada at the GP Quebec and Montreal, winning the former and taking fifth in the latter as he showed mixed form. But what's certain is that with both he and Van Aert in the same team, they only become more dangerous as threats to win solo or from a sprint, as shown in the Paris Olympics or Wollongong '22, where Evenepoel claimed the victories.National coach Serge Pauwels will have his hands full formulating just how they take things on in two weeks, with the final not set to be laid out to the riders until those who have been racing the Vuelta arrive."Wout arrives next Tuesday [September 22], so we still have 5-6 days before the World Championships. That is enough time to put our heads together," said Pauwels to national broadcaster ."The World Championships are ridden without earpieces, so little can be adjusted during the race. The riders will have to anticipate the changing conditions in the race."Wout rode a very strong Vuelta. He will be ready in two weeks, because riders like that usually reach a peak in form in the week to two or three weeks after a Grand Tour. That works out perfectly for him, just as it does for Thibau Nys and Gianni Vermeersch, who will complete our selection in Canada in nine days."Thibau Nys offers full support for two all-time greatsNys will travel to Montreal on the same day as Van Aert, and after battling his way through illness and injury to even make it to the start of the Vuelta in Monaco on August 22, he had to fight even more to make it all the way to the Granada finale. "If you had shown me the results of this Vuelta before the season, I would not have been happy or not be satisfied with it, but according to all the setbacks I had: the knee surgery, then the sickness before the Vuelta, and the heat stroke during the Vuelta, I would say I'm satisfied," Nys told before the last stage. "I'm happy with the two third places I got; the second one especially was quite a strong effort," – losing out to Van Aert from a breakaway into Córdoba – "But it's been a bit of mixed feelings. "I found myself really growing in shape in the first two weeks, and then the heat stroke came just before the second rest day, and there was a small setback. Since then, I found myself not really improving anymore, but feeling the tiredness in my body coming up. So I'm looking forward a lot to a few easy days now."Montreal will see Nys' debut in the elite men's road race at the World Championships, having finished sixth as an under-23 back in 2021 in Leuven, and he will make up part of Belgium's supporting cast alongside Vermeersch, Tiesj Benoot, Alec Segaert, Maxim Van Gils, and Quinten Hermans."I'm looking forward to it a lot. It looks like Wout and Remco are in incredible shape at the moment," said Nys. "It's been spectacular to view also from the race itself. Even now, when they're still active riders, they will for sure go down as some of the biggest stars in the history of cycling, and to be riding with them, it's a big honour as well. I will just really try to be at my best level, at my best game, and prove that I can be helpful."While the absence of Tadej Pogačar after his crash at the Vuelta leaves the Belgians as the likely favourites in Montreal, they know that winning the race will require them to beat almost all of the other top riders in the world. They won't be taking their status for granted. "I think Del Toro and Seixas are the biggest competitors. Pidcock is also in top form," said national coach Pauwels. "And then there is Mathieu van der Poel. There is still a bit more of a question mark behind his form. He will still ride the Tour of Luxembourg. But you always have to reckon with him. If he makes the trip to Canada, it won't be to fill out the peloton."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Blue Jays loss leads to Yanks’ playoff clinch
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: The Yankees were the only member of the top trio of American League teams playing on Monday, with both the Rays and Red Sox off inadvance of series against the A’s and Rangers, respectively. The AL West-leading [read: .500] Astros were also sidelined. So yeah, if the 2026 Yankees are the gold standard, then you know it’s a dreary night of action. Thankfully, they took care of their own business after a slow start by dropping a six-spot in the eighth inning on their ol’ Twins pals in the eighth inning to win on Clinching Day.As it turned out though, the Yankees had already punched their 61st ticket to the postseason! Here’s what the teams that active were up to on Monday night.Chicago White Sox (77-73) 7, Cleveland Guardians (76-75) 3Separated by a half-game before first pitch, the White Sox and Guardians squared off in Cleveland to begin a three-game set that could decide both the AL Central and—believe it or not with these records—a first-round bye. It was a scoreless duel through five, with Guardos ace Gavin Williams and the opener/bulk guy combo of Sean Newcomb and Sean Burke putting goose eggs on the board. Williams returned to the mound in the sixth, looking for a couple more punchouts to tie and surpass both Dylan Cease and Jacob Misiorowski (236) for the MLB lead. Instead, was the one who got punc—OK you get it.It started innocently enough with an infield hit by Andrew Benintendi. Then came one of the most remarkable at-bats of the entire season, as Tristan Peters worked Williams for 18 pitches before taking a walk. It was the longest at-bat (well, plate appearance I suppose) since a 19-pitch battle by Matt Wieters for the 2020 Cardinals (sure?).Peters had worked Williams’ pitch count up to 113 by that point, so he was done for the night. Tim Herrin replaced him, and he honestly did his job by getting a double-play ball to first baseman Nathaniel Lowe. But Lowe’s throw to second caromed off Peters’ helmet and scored Benintendi for the first run of the game.From there, the wheels came off. Chase Meidroth singled in a second, Randal Grichuk got a knock to load the bases, Kyle Teel doubled in a pair, and after Daniel Espino replaced Herrin, Miguel Vargas dropped the hammer with a two-run bomb:Burke gave one back in the home half and David Fry at least briefly woke up the home crowd with a two-run homer with two down in the ninth, but this never felt close after that one inning. Final score: 7-3, Chicago, and a 1.5-game lead in the AL Central.Toronto Blue Jays (75-76) 5, Detroit Tigers (71-79) 6: Most Yankees fans’ eyes were directed at this game though, as either a Jays loss or Yankees win would punch the Bombers’ ticket to the postseason. They got both! The Jays’ loss came a little less than half an hour before New York beat Minnesota, so the Yanks got to feel good in the dugout for just a bit before they celebrated on the field.For awhile, it looked like the wait would continue until at least tomorrow, as the Yanks trailed the Twins 2-1 through seven while the Jays rallied against the Tigers. Detroit had taken a 4-2 lead in the seventh with José Soriano set his no-hit bid ablaze, as Max Clark and Spencer Torkelson both doubled to get the Tigers ahead. But a three-run blast by Kazuma Okamoto brought the Jays back in front, 5-4. A year ago, this probably would’ve been a propeller of sorts; however, these Jays are not the same, and neither is weary Louie Varland. A pair of hits off Joe Mantiply set up the game-tying Tigers attack in the eighth on a flare to left by Brett Callahan against Varland, and a leadoff walk put Varland in position to fumble the ball away as the go-ahead run crossed home.After his own leadoff walk, Kenley Jansen struck out Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and got Alejandro Kirk to bounce into a game-ending double play for his 496th career save. The Jays still trail the Guardians by a game in the AL Wild Card with the Rangers one win behind them.Baltimore Orioles (73-78) 2, New York Mets (69-81) 1: The O’s are just barely alive in this Wild Card conversation as well, but they got the win they needed to get to three games back; they’ll need many more this week! This one was all about Pete Alonso’s long-awaited return to Queens, and the Mets fans showered him with affection on a night in which they were (appropriately) eliminated. Alonso took an oh-fer, but Gunnar Henderson broke a 1-1 tie in the eighth with a solo shot and Rico Garcia held on to close it out.

item.title: This 'fix' wouldn't have saved F1's Spanish GP
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: The failure of the Spanish Grand Prix to produce the kind of spectacle offered by other Formula 1 races this year has inevitably focused on the lack of overtaking opportunities around the Madring circuit.Combined entries, barrier pinch points and a lack of wide, heavy braking zones - especially at Turn 5 - all contributed to making it extremely difficult to pass a rival.It is little wonder, as The Race revealed on Sunday, that Madring chiefs are already planning changes to three key corners for 2027 with the expectation that next year's race produces a bit more of a show.But it was not just the track layout that contributed to a lack of action, as another factor in how things played out was that there was not much strategic variation either.Even the most boring of track layouts can deliver thrillers if tyre strategy gets blown open.Make the fastest route to the chequered flag unclear and you get teams taking different approaches, plus the kinds of pace offset that create the circumstances for wheel-to-wheel action.The hard tyre's durabilityThe Madring delivered one of those Monaco/Sochi-style phenomena where the hard tyre (the C2 compound in Spain) was good enough to last the whole race - as Pierre Gasly proved by waiting until the penultimate lap for his mandatory compound switch to get off what he had started the race with.After tongue-in-cheek claims after first running on Friday of a potential six-stopper being on the cards, based on the high levels of degradation seen, the transformation into an easy one-stopper was remarkable.Haas driver Esteban Ocon said the behaviour of the tyres was one of the limiting factors in why there was not much action in the race, because drivers could push on without fear of excessive degradation as long as they did not spend too much time in the dirty air of the car ahead."The thing is that it was so consistent, the tyres on the second stint, that as soon as you were following another car, you were losing so much grip," he said."When I was doing blue flags to other cars, I was losing half a second, seven tenths easily. And then after it was coming back because it was all about overheating."As soon as the overheating was coming down, you had pace again. So that's why there was no overtaking. It was too fast, the pace, basically."It was like 120% from as soon as you pitted to the end. And because the graining didn't happen, that's where we ended up. If we had a race on Friday, it would have been much better!"This outcome has inevitably prompted questions about whether the Madring spectacle would have been more entertaining had the tyre compounds been a bit more on the aggressive side.It is a nice theory that if you took away the comfort of the thermal and mechanical robustness of the C2 hard tyre the Spanish GP would have been better.That suggests that, forced onto softer compounds, drivers would have had a more challenging time in having rubber that did not last the whole distance, thereby producing more excitement.The idea is good, but sadly reality bites when it comes to understanding the complex factors that dictate whether races become strategic masterclasses.First, there is a notable difference in behaviour and characteristics between the C2 and the C3, which means that, while the hard was good for the whole race, the medium was significantly not as good and much more prone to the risk of graining.As McLaren's Oscar Piastri said: "The medium tyre was just awful. It was good for literally one lap, but then it was terrible."Increased degradation does not automatically mean more stops though. It can (especially when overtaking is difficult) lead to more tyre management and cars running well off the pace, and you end up with the same spectacle as we got on Sunday.Plus, one important element at Madring that will forever speak against multi-stop races is the length of the pitlane.Swapping tyres there costs around 25 seconds - one of the biggest losses of the season - so teams are always going to try to minimise the need to change tyres.Based on the evidence from the Madring, Pirelli felt that going a step softer with the compounds - bringing the C3/C4/C5 rather than the C2/C3/C4 - was not a way to improve the spectacle.That is because, as Pirelli's head of motorsport, Dario Marrafuschi, pointed out, based on the struggles that drivers had with the C3 and C4 in the short stints in which they managed to keep them alive in the race, it would have simply turned the race into a major management drama.Throw into the mix too that the Madring, thanks to the banked La Monumental and high numbers of corners, is one of the most challenging tracks on the calendar for tyres, then it would also increase the possibility of safety dangers thanks to the high levels of wear."It would have been a two-stop race with a high wear," Marrafuschi told The Race. "On paper you can say, 'OK, it must be a two-stopper'."But, because of traffic, drivers would just end up doing what Gasly did."It was a good choice to have the C2 as a race compound and give teams the possibility to have one-stop in case of an early safety car. The C3/C4/C5 would have been too much."Going softer would also have caused trouble in qualifying. As it was, the C4 teams took into the fight for grid positions was screaming from overheating doing a single push lap.The C5 would probably have fallen off a cliff and been pretty useless.Marrafuschi added: "Even during one lap with the soft, after La Monumental, the overheating of the rear was there. If the soft was a C5, maybe you would run the risk of thermal degradation during qualifying as well. It wouldn't pay the bill."The reality is that the margins between a race delivering a perfect strategy mix of different approaches, a nailed on easy one-stopper, and complete chaos are sometimes not very much.With Madrid's track being super-smooth, and offering high grip, teams knew going into the race that if they could avoid the risk of graining, then the one-stop strategy was on.If not, as one engineer said, then it would instead have turned into a chaotic, heavy-degradation, two-stop-plus graining fest.While the latter may sound exciting, it actually risks producing something that is equally as bad: one of those grands prix where there is just an endless cycle of stops so the race has no narrative.Some of the nailed-on elements of Madring - the smooth, high-grip surface, the forces through La Monumental, and the long pitlane - mean that unless overtaking opportunities are improved there is little that can be done to encourage more stops.All eyes are on what track changes are done next year because opening the door for passes will be the best way to improve the strategy element too.

item.title: Trump EPA moves to wipe out climate rules for power plants
item.author: Liza Gross, Inside Climate News
item.content:encoded: On the heels of the hottest summer on record and a United Nations report warning that global temperatures are likely to push climate risks to “increasingly dangerous heights,” the Trump administration overturned most of a Biden-era rule limiting climate pollution from power plants, the second-largest source of greenhouse gas emissions.The Environmental Protection Agency announced a final plan Monday that guts the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, which the agency said exceeds its authority under the Clean Air Act by requiring control technologies “that are not adequately demonstrated.” The agency also proposed revoking “all remaining GHG emissions requirements for power plants,” arguing their emissions “have no material impact on climate change.”The plan to revoke the Carbon Pollution Standards was initially revealed last spring.

item.title: 'It's a strange dynamic' – Finn Fisher-Black argues lack of funding from Cycling New Zealand for riders at Road World Championships can change approach to race
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: New Zealand rider Finn Fisher-Black has said there's no change this year to the NZ Cycling Federation's policy of not funding their elite riders' costs at the upcoming Road World Championships, with the 24-year-old and other elite pros paying their way to Canada to participate.Following a second place in the Tour de Pologne, Fisher-Black has just completed a Vuelta a España, having supported team leader Primož Roglič throughout the three weeks while finishing in 52nd place himself.Speaking during the race to , Fisher-Black said he was looking forward to his third elite Road World Championships participation and hoping that he might be in the running for a top ten place in the elite men's road race.However, while New Zealand's elite men's side will be six strong and the elite women's team will have four riders in their line-up, Fisher-Black pointed out that the lack of funding had not changed despite his sister Niamh, a racer with Lidl-Trek, taking silver in the Worlds last year.The lack of funds created a "strange dynamic," Fisher-Black said, and meant that riders were acting more self-interestedly as a result, although personal friendships did reduce any potential friction."It's a strange dynamic for NZ because we don't get funding from Cycling New Zealand; we all pay to be there, so it's also a strange dynamic, like we all kind of also want to do our own race," Fisher-Black told ."But we're all good mates from New Zealand so it'll probably be about looking each other during the race and try to have numbers during the final and take it from there.The lack of funding for the Kiwi road squad was first reported in 2022, and it would appear there has been no change in the New Zealand federation's policy of putting all available expenditure elsewhere since then. Much of the available budget, according to Fisher-Black, goes on the track team."It came in a few years ago, like, pretty much when I started doing the elite Worlds, they stopped the funding. It's just the structure of Cycling New Zealand because they prioritise the track and the road; there's no funding."We also do what we can, my sister [Niamh] was second last year [in the elite women's road race] so you'd think there'd maybe be some change, but for the moment it's the same."We have to do it like that, and we're fortunate that for the rest of the year we have a lot of support from our teams."Fisher-Black is part of a six-man elite men's squad with the most experienced racer, George Bennett (NSN), whose best result was 18th a few years back. The other four are debutants Josh Kench (Groupama-FDJ United) and Ben Oliver (Modern Adventure), while Laurence Pithie (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and Corbin Strong (NSN) have one participation at senior level.Fisher-Black himself is looking to see how he feels after the Vuelta, where he was one of the most active elements in Roglič's squad in the mountains and on the flat, culminating in a long break on the final day through the Sierra Nevada last Saturday."In some ways, it's been a big training camp here, and I hope I come out well," Fisher-Black said during the race's second week. "A lot of the time coming through a Grand Tour, your body feels a bit cooked, and as soon as it stops, your body shuts down. So I'll try to keep the body ticking over a bit and then go on to the Worlds where we'll have a good race there. We'll have a strong team."His own goals in the Montreal hilly circuit – the kind of terrain where he's shone in the past – are to follow the wheeltracks of retired fastman Julian Dean, the only elite men's racer from New Zealand to break into the top ten at the road worlds this side of 2000 with a ninth and a tenth place to his name."I'd love to go there and be fighting for the top 10," Fisher-Black said. "It'd be nice just to be in the final."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia.
