item.title: Antonelli wins first Madrid F1 race after Norris VSC blow
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli won the first-ever Formula 1 race at the Madring, as Lando Norris and McLaren lost a likely victory due to their pitstop timing.Norris led away from pole, with Antonelli only briefly jumping ahead twice when he ran off the circuit on lap one, before returning the lead to Norris on both occasions. The McLaren driver was looking comfortable until Lance Stroll brought his Aston Martin to a halt in the run-off area at Turn 20. That triggered a virtual safety car, but Norris had already passed the pit entry by then, while Antonelli - as well as Max Verstappen and George Russell behind - were able to make their pitstop under the VSC.Norris pitted a lap later, but the race was back under green flag conditions. The pitstop was slow too (seven seconds), so he was jumped by Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell. Charles Leclerc didn't pit, so he led more laps of the race than any other driver before finally trading in his hard tyres on lap 48 of 57, allowing Antonelli to claim a race lead he'd never relinquish.Verstappen finished second, having lost out to Antonelli on the opening lap.He'd passed him and Lewis Hamilton on the first lap to run second behind Norris, but he overtook the latter by missing the first chicane to avoid Hamilton's Ferrari.Much to Verstappen's dissatisfaction, Red Bull ordered him to give the place back to Hamilton - but Verstappen lost out to Antonelli too because he'd passed Hamilton. "He can give me the position now, f***ing bullshit. F***ing mickey-mouse racing this is,” Verstappen told his team at the time. Hamilton's race didn't last much longer than that as he retired with brake problems. Norris had to settle for third place despite a penultimate lap attack on Verstappen, while they were lapping a scrapping Arvid Lindblad and Nico Hulkenberg.Verstappen had to cut a chicane, and while he was noted for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, it was quickly dismissed as needing no further investigation.He finished ahead of Leclerc, who didn't get the safety car intervention Ferrari was hoping for. Russell was fifth, having stopped for a second time and lost the position he gained on Norris with his VSC pitstop.Stand-in Liam Lawson earned his best result for Red Bull so far in sixth place ahead of Franco Colapinto, who won F1's midfield scrap and even beat McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Lindblad was ninth for Racing Bulls, having triumphed in a tight duel with Hulkenberg's Audi, in the points for the third time in four races. Along with Hamilton and Stroll, home hero Carlos Sainz retired - but not before picking up a five-second time penalty for clashing with fellow Spaniard Fernando Alonso - as did Sergio Perez's Cadillac.1 Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)2 Max Verstappen (Red Bull) +4.4s3 Lando Norris (McLaren) +5.1s4 Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) +29.1s5 George Russell (Mercedes) +29.8s6 Liam Lawson (Red Bull) +1m26.7s7 Franco Colapinto (Alpine) +1m34.3s8 Oscar Piastri (McLaren) +1m35.8s9 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +1 lap10 Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) +1 lap11 Esteban Ocon (Haas) +1 lap12 Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) +1 lap13 Pierre Gasly (Alpine) +1 lap14 Yuki Tsunoda (Racing Bulls) +1 lap15 Alexander Albon (Williams) +1 lap16 Oliver Bearman (Haas) +1 lap17 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +2 laps18 Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) +3 lapsDNF Carlos Sainz (Williams)DNF Sergio Perez (Cadillac)DNF Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)DNF Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari)

item.title: F1 Spanish GP: Antonelli wins after Norris loses out under VSC

item.title: Arvid de Klijn sprints to glory at the GP de Fourmies
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Arvid de Kleijn (Tudor) won the GP de Fourmies for the second time in his career after proving to be the strongest from the mass sprint finish to end the 200km one-day race.The Dutchman beat Tobias Müller (Unibet Rose Rockets) and Ethan Vernon (NSN) to the line at the head of the peloton, while Pavel Bittner (Picnic-PostNL) and Matteo Moschetti (Pinarello.Q36.5) rounded out the top five.The victory marks De Kleijn's first in almost a year, with his most recent triumph coming at the Tour de Langkawi last OctoberThe day's breakaway was caught 35km from the line, with Javier Serrano (Polti-VisitMalta) the strongest of the group and the final survivor of the five-man move.From there, it was always going to be a sprint finish given the nature of the course and multiple teams interested in a bunch finish. That didn't put off several attackers, including Clément Dubois (Van Rysel Roubaix), Florian Sénéchal (Alpecin-Premier Tech), and Jonas Abrahamsen (Uno-X Mobility), however.In the end, none of the attacks managed to get clear of the surging peloton, and so it was teams including Soudal-QuickStep and Uno-X Mobility who led the way to the line for the sprint finish.A crash in the peloton 400 metres from the line didn't disrupt those at the very front, including De Kleijn, who possessed the fastest finish from a large group to take his 19th career victorytFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Faun Tour Femmes: Lauren Dickson takes first professional victory on stage 4 as team-mate Juliette Berthet seals overall
item.author: Dan Challis
item.content:encoded: Lauren Dickson attacked with 4km to go to win the final stage of Faun Tour Femmes 2026, claiming the first professional victory of her career. Her FDJ United-SUEZ team-mate, Juliette Berthet, sealed the overall victory.The Scottish rider had been distanced due to an acceleration by Niamh Fisher-Black (Lidl-Trek) on the final climb of the day, but caught back up to the lead before attacking solo all the way to the line in Peyrus,. Berthet finished the stage in second place to claim the second stage race victory of her career. Fisher-Black was third on the stage and second overall after an impressive climbing display. Dickson finished the race in third on general classification.There was nothing to separate Berthet and Niamh Fisher-Black going into the final stage with the overall classification set to be decided on the final and most mountainous stage of the race. The 135km course took in two laps of a circuit including the 11.7km Col de Tourniol and the shorter Col de Limouches. Fisher-Black accelerated away from the FDJ United-SUEZ duo of Berthet and Dickson in the final kilometres of the second pass of the Tourniol. Dickson kept Fisher-Black’s advantage small before closing just before the top of the climb. The New Zealander tried again on the Col de Limouches, distancing Dickson but not Berthet. Dickson chased back on the descent and attacked off the front with 4km left, building a significant lead as Fisher-Black pursued with Berthet on her wheel. Dickson held strong to take the win. Behind, Berthet rounded Fisher-Black in the closing metres to crown a dominant FDJ United-SUEZ performance. For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: As it happened: final win goes to the breakaway on stage 21 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to the final stage of the 2026 Vuelta a España. September 13, 2026 – 10:08 AMAfter yesterday's epic slog in the mountains, which saw a thrilling battle for both the GC placings and the stage win, the Vuelta comes to an end with a much more straightforward, simple stage.It's not necessarily one for the sprinters, however. There's a testing climb in the final circuit in Granada which looks set to make this a fascinatingly balanced battle for the stage win.September 13, 2026 – 10:14 AMDespite that climb in the finishing circuit, it does not look as though the stage is going to be raced for GC, following the announcement that the times will be neutralised by the final lap. The riders have cited safety concerns as the reason for the change. September 13, 2026 – 10:18 AMHaving been under so much pressure this past week or so, today is at last a chance for Enric Mas to celebrate. This is the day his whole career has been building towards; after four podium finishes at past editions of the Vuelta, and so many more in other races, he can at last call himself a Grand Tour champion.September 13, 2026 – 10:28 AMThe riders are at the unofficial start, and five men who are set to retire are being honoured - Pello Bilbao, Jesus Herrada, David de la Cruz, Steven Kruijswijk and Magnus Cort - the latter of which addressed the crowd earlier. September 13, 2026 – 10:33 AMAnd they're off! Albeit to a slow start, as the end-of-term celebrations commence. Mas and his Movistar team are the first to move ahead of the front of the peloton for their photo, riding arm in arm in custom red jerseys. September 13, 2026 – 10:39 AMWhile the opening of the stage will be more of a celebration than a race, there are endless stories to unpack from yesterday’s thriller. There might not have been any major changes in the GC, barring Sepp Kuss’ rise to fifth place, but the stage really did have everything.September 13, 2026 – 10:45 AMOne rider who is not present to celebrate finishing the Vuelta is Eddie Dunbar. The Irishman crashed out of the race yesterday, but does at least go home as a stage winner after his triumph in the mountains two days ago. September 13, 2026 – 10:50 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 13, 2026 – 10:57 AMPrimož Roglič might have failed to take the red jersey from Enric Mas yesterday, but he still looks in good spirits, giving a wave to the TV moto, and chatting and enjoying himself with his companions in the peloton. September 13, 2026 – 11:04 AMHere's a look at the snazzy jerseys the Movistar riders have rocked up in for today's stage, to celebrate Mas' overall victory. September 13, 2026 – 11:07 AMThe riders are still ambling along at a slow pace as they make their way towards the circuit in Granada. They are still assembling in team formation to have their photo taken, and there's no sign of a race breaking out any time soon.September 13, 2026 – 11:16 AMHere was the retiring riders receiving their guard of honour at the start of the stage, led by Steven Kruijswijk. This will be the last day of racing in the Dutchman's long career, a memorable which saw him star in the mountains early on, nearly win the Giro d'Italia, podium at the Tour de France, and then win multiple Grand Tours as a rebranded domestique for Visma. He'll be sorely missed.September 13, 2026 – 11:21 AMThe festivities appear to be finished for now, and Movistar have moved to the front of the peloton to increase the pace a little. It's still more of an amble than a race, but the battle for the stage win will initiate at some point.September 13, 2026 – 11:30 AMThis year's Vuelta podium, al of whom look happy with their finish.For Mas and Roglič, it's a respective five and six time they've finished on the podium here, but for Gall it's a first. He had to dig deep yesterday to defend from an onslaught of attacks from the man directly beneath him on GC, Richard Carapaz.September 13, 2026 – 11:37 AMAn excellent Vuelta got even better for Visma-Lease a Bike yesterday, when Sepp Kuss propelled himself up to fifth overall with a brilliant long-range attack. The team aren’t done yet, either, and will be gunning for an eighth stage win today, with either of their two stars Brennan or Van Aert. September 13, 2026 – 11:49 AMThere still haven't been any attacks out of the peloton, as Movistar set a gentle pace towards the start of the finishing circuit in Granada. Upon arriving, they will do four laps, where the race for the stage win will take off.September 13, 2026 – 11:54 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 13, 2026 – 12:04 PMOscar Onley was one of the riders to lose a place on GC yesterday to Sepp Kuss, slipping to 6th place, but nevertheless completes what has been a successful Grand Tour thanks to victory in the young riders classification. He's had to overcome some hardship to do so, too, having been ill earlier in the race; to pull off such a result in these circumstances is further proof of his great talent. September 13, 2026 – 12:13 PMOf all the many storylines to follow during yesterday's stage, perhaps the most heart-warming was Mikel Landa's stage win. For all his talent and brilliant performances over the years, he hasn't actually won that much at this high a level, and certainly not in recent years. It will surely go down as one of the best days of his career. September 13, 2026 – 12:22 PMAbove all, today is for Enric Mas. Up until he has had a career of near-misses and runner-up finishes, and spoke candidly yesterday about how hard he has had to work to deliver this victory. Chapeau.September 13, 2026 – 12:30 PMThere are still a lot of teams without a stage win at this Vuelta, will be desperate to do so today. Unusually, Lidl-Trek and Alpecin-Premier Tech are both without one, contrary to how they usually perform, as are NSN, Jayco-AlUla, Astana, Picnic PosnNL, Lotto Intermarché and the wildcard teams Burgos BH and Equipo Kern Pharma. And although they have high placings on GC to celebrate, Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe, Decathlon, EF Education-EasyPost and Netcompany are also lacking one. September 13, 2026 – 12:40 PMThis year’s Vuelta is set to come to a close, but there was news today of next year's race. The Gran Partida is set to take place in Galicia, the first time it has been held on Spanish roads for a few years. September 13, 2026 – 12:42 PMHere we go, the riders are at last in the finishing circuit in Granada! They pass through the finish line for the first time, to huge crowds who have taken to the roadside. Despite this, the pace is still steady, the race having not yet ignited. It's difficult to know what to expect after the final lap's time neutralisation, and so far there hasn't been an interest in racing. September 13, 2026 – 12:48 PMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 13, 2026 – 12:54 PMStill no attacks forthcoming in the peloton. The pace is up, as Movistar continue to ride at the front of the peloton, but nobody is taking the race on.September 13, 2026 – 12:58 PMLots of teams are moving up to the front now, as the peloton is spread across the road. Still no attacks, but some riders appear to be readying themselves, and are fighting to position. September 13, 2026 – 1:02 PMThe race is heating up now. Visma-Lease a Bike first took control at the front of the peloton, with Steven Kruijswijk, riding on the last day of his career. And now Groupama-FDJ take over as they take on the circuit's climb for the second of four times. At the back, one of the key sprinters is struggling - Jordi Meeus.September 13, 2026 – 1:04 PMGroupama's Tronchon has caused a split over the top of the climb, taking a handful of riders with him, including Brennan, Paret-Peintre, Romele and Van Aert. September 13, 2026 – 1:08 PMA group of eight have gone clear - Brennan, Nys, Paret-Peintre, Laurance, Romele, Fisher-Black, Tronchon and Vader. There's a large group behind (featuring Van Aert, who didn't quite make the split).September 13, 2026 – 1:13 PMIt's actually nine men in the lead group - Léo Bisiaux is present too. Behind a chase group is only ten seconds adrift, and chasing hard, as they cross the finish line for the third time - two more laps to go.The peloton led by Movistar is further behind, and prioritising safety rather then chasing the stage win. September 13, 2026 – 1:19 PMThe break has been caught by the chase group, and attacks are coming thick and fast, but nobody is clear at the moment.September 13, 2026 – 1:22 PMThe front group is large in size as they race towards the final lap. There are no attacks at the moment - they're waiting presumably for the final ascent of the climb. Meanwhile the peloton is 1:18 behind, being led by Movistar. September 13, 2026 – 1:26 PMThe riders hear the bell for the last lap! Bahrain Victorious lead the front group over the line, looking to set up Pello Bilbao. This is going to be an intense one, with multiple riders still in contention for the stage win. Everything is going to explode in a few kilometres when they start the climb. September 13, 2026 – 1:29 PMBilbao took on the climb with a massive attack, and has a lead of several seconds. Netompany are leading the chase.Riders are being shelled out the back of the group, including Van Aert and Coquard. September 13, 2026 – 1:31 PMLaurance attacked out the peloton, and has caught and passed Bilbao, who went very deep with that attack.Riders continue to be dropped from the chase group, which is getting smaller and smaller - and Brennan is among those to have been left behind!September 13, 2026 – 1:33 PMLaurance has been caught by a group of about fifteen that have come together on the descent. And Brennan is back among them. There's no way the others will want to take him to a sprint, and indeed they are already attacking each other, with Nys trying a move. September 13, 2026 – 1:37 PMAttacks keep coming, and four riders have managed to get a gap with 2km to go: Debruyne, Romele, Laurance and Johannessen. The rest are leaning on Brennan to chase them down. September 13, 2026 – 1:38 PMLaurance has been dropped, it appears the stage win will go to one of the other three...September 13, 2026 – 1:40 PMJohannessen takes the sprint, ahead of more recognised fastman Romele. It's a really close call but the Astana rider get quite had the energy to pass him at the line. September 13, 2026 – 1:44 PMNow the peloton arrives at the finish, lapping up the atmosphere and waving to the crowd, who are making a huge noise. Mostly for Enric Mas - the Spanish have turned out in numbers to celebrate their first home winner since 2014.September 13, 2026 – 1:47 PMThat victory was a long time coming, whose second-place finish yesterday was his third in Grand Tours this season alone, in addition to many more runner-up finishes at World Tour level.It comes in unlikely circumstances, too, for a rider renowned for his climbing above all else. September 13, 2026 – 1:52 PMSpare a thought for Romele, who looked devastated at the finish, holding his head in his hands. He has been one of the breakthrough riders of this Vuelta, and came so close to ending it with a stage win. Sprinting, climbing, attacking - the Italian has it all, and is some talent. September 13, 2026 – 1:58 PMJob done for Movistar! There were doubts about their ability to defend the red jersey when they so suddenly and surprisingly inherited it from Tadej Pogačar, but they handled whatever was thrown at them, and passed the rest with flying colours. September 13, 2026 – 2:07 PMA familiar sight from this year's Vuelta, and especially today - Enric Mas' beaming smile. His final margin of victory over Primož Roglič was 2:15, September 13, 2026 – 2:13 PMPrimož Roglič settles for second overall, but doesn't look too disappointed at the finish. Though he would dearly have wanted that record-breaking fifth Vuelta victory, considering where his form has been all year, second place is a very impressive result nevertheless. September 13, 2026 – 2:20 PMStage winner Tobias Halland Johannessen, in front of the striking podium backdrop in Granada.September 13, 2026 – 2:25 PMKing of the Mountains winner Santiago Buitrago.September 13, 2026 – 2:27 PMWhite jersey winner Oscar Onley.September 13, 2026 – 2:28 PMPoints classification winner Wout van Aert.September 13, 2026 – 2:30 PMAnd finally, the red jersey winner Enric Mas.September 13, 2026 – 2:36 PMThanks for joining us today, and for the Vuelta as a whole In terms of pure unpredictability, it’s been one of the most exciting Grand Tours in recent years, and has delivered great drama in terms of attacking racing, spectacular performances, and the daily fights for stage wins. That's it for the Grand Tour season, but not the cycling season as a whole, with the smaller matter of the World Championships coming up in just over a week. Be sure to check out our comprehensive coverage of it, and all the other cycling taking place across the globe.

item.title: Matthews, Gigante, Hindley headline experienced Australian squads for Montreal Road World Championships
item.author: Dan Challis
item.content:encoded: Having recently made her return to racing after more than a year away from the peloton, Sarah Gigante (AG Insurance-Soudal) is the stand-out name among the women’s team on a climber’s course, which will suit her strengths. Though, only four of Australia's six quota spots have been filled for the women's elite road race. Veteran Amanda Spratt (Lidl-Trek) is among those who will travel to Montreal, taking part in her final Worlds before she retires at the end of this season. Georgia Baker (Liv-AlUla-Jayco) and Lauretta Hanson (Lidl-Trek) will support Gigante and Spratt.“Although Sarah has had very few race days this year, she’s proven her exceptional ability to overcome adversity,” AusCycling’s Head Coach of Endurance, Conor Taylor, said in a press release.“We know that a fit and healthy Sarah can be extremely competitive on a tough World Championship course like the one in Montréal.”Former Worlds medallists Ben O’Connor and Michael Matthews (both Jayco-AlUla) form part of the Australian elite men’s team, which is stacked with climbing talent. Michael Storer (Tudor), Jai Hindley and Luke Tuckwell (both Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) are all suited to the challenging course around Montréal. Taylor noted the absence of Jay Vine (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) in the lineup due to his recent illness. “The loss of Jay is of course a blow to the team, but of course, his health comes first, and we wish him the best with his recovery,” Taylor said.“Jay’s absence, however, presents a great opportunity for another rider to contribute towards what’s historically been an extremely competitive mixed relay team.”Several promising riders will also take part in the under-23 and junior categories. The likes of Talia Appleton (Liv-AlUla-Jayco), 2023 junior world time trial champion Felicity Wilson-Haffenden (Lidl-Trek) and Emily Dixon (Canyon-SRAM Generation) can be expected to challenge in the women’s under-23 events. Likewise, Cameron Rogers (Netcompany-Ineos Racing Academy) and Jack Ward (Lidl-Trek Future Racing) in the men’s under-23 race.As ever, the Australians will target the mixed relay. Having won the 2024 and 2025 editions, a strong team will look to become the first to win the event on three occasions. However, several former members of previous mixed relay squads will miss the Worlds, including Vine, Brodie Chapman (UAE Team L'IMAD) and Luke Plapp (Jayco-AlUla).“A strong result in the team time trial is certainly a major objective for this Australian squad. There will likely be a couple of debutants in the relay line-up in Montréal with a mix of elite and under-23 representation, which is exciting,” Taylor said.“Despite the key absences, we believe we have a squad ready for the demands of these World Championships and that the selections reflect a genuine ambition to win medals across the time trials and road races.”For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Vuelta a España Grand Depart returns to home soil with start in Galicia in 2027
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: After three foreign starts in Lisbon, Turin and Monaco, the opening stage of the 2027 Vuelta a España will see the race return to Spain, with the Grand Depart due to take place in Santiago de Compostela in Galicia on September 4. The announcement was made in a short ceremony before the final stage of 2026, which started in Carrefour Granada.The 2027 race will begin with a road stage in Santiago de Compostela, which most recently hosted a Vuelta stage in 2021, when the race concluded there with a time trial won by Primož Roglič.Adriano Malori, Oscar Freire, and Alex Zülle have also won in Santiago de Compostela through the years, while the town has featured in several recent editions of O Gran Camiño, too.The 2027 Vuelta start in Galicia has been scheduled to coincide with one of Galicia's most important religious festivals, the 'Xacobeo Year', which forms part of a special celebration of the Santiago de Compostela Pilgrimage seven times each century.Next year's Vuelta will start on Saturday, September 4 and will then see the race return to the Spanish capital of Madrid for its usual finish on Sunday, September 26.2028 is expected to see the Vuelta have another foreign start, this time in Sardinia, Italy.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'It's no gift, it's thanks to his hard work' – Spain's last Vuelta a España winner Alberto Contador pays tribute to Enric Mas as 2026 victory nears for successor
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: Spain's last Vuelta a España winner Alberto Contador has paid tribute to the rider set to be his successor this Sunday in Granada, with Enric Mas just hours away from overall victory in his home Grand Tour.Contador took Spain's previous Vuelta win in 2014, just a few months after breaking his tibia at the Tour de France, a race he looked set to win for a third time.Following his injury, 'El Pistolero' bounced back on home soil, taking a resounding triumph ahead of the rider who dominated Grand Tours that decade, Chris Froome.Mas' victory comes after the top rider in the world, Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG), had to pull out of the Vuelta after crashing and breaking his collarbone on stage 8, when he was comfortably leading the race and looked set to hold top spot all the way to the finish.However, as Contador pointed out, Mas mounted a solid defence of the red jersey after inheriting the lead when Pogačar pulled out, and after four podium finishes in the Vuelta, his victory is well deserved."When we have riders like [Jonas] Vingegaard (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Pogačar in a Grand Tour, they practically block it," Contador told . "And that's normal."They are very consistent riders who don't have off-days, and in that sense, they limit things a lot."But there's a whole line of riders who want to be up there in the next spot available, second overall, and this time a Grand Tour lead became 'vacant', and Enric seized that opportunity."That's not a gift; it's thanks to his hard work and his form. He was the strongest."Quite apart from his physical condition, Contador argued that Mas' ability to keep himself from getting distracted by social media and external noise was an important factor in staying on track and maintaining a firm grip overall all the way from stage 8 to the finish in Granada."To do that [win the Vuelta], you have to stay strong, believe in yourself and your own possibilities, and detach yourself from what people are saying. That's easier said than done these days because of social media, but Enric's a good example of how to achieve that."Mas is ending an 11-year drought of Grand Tour wins for Spain, and 12 years without any Spanish triumphs in the Vuelta a España – by far the longest in its history, with the previous biggest gap being the near-decade between Angelino Soler's victory in 1961 and Luis Ocaña's in 1970."I didn't expect it to be so long because at that point [2014] we were part of a generation that won a lot of races," Contador said. "If it wasn't one rider it was another; we were favourites in the Worlds and in the Grand Tours, even in Classics, and we'd taken quite a few Tours [de France] in a short space of time. It was normal to think that we'd continue with that run of success."Instead, over a decade has passed, and it has taken Mas, 31 years old and once seen as Contador's heir apparent, to end the lengthy absence of Spanish Grand Tour wins. Contador recollected that Mas had shown considerable promise as a young racer, riding with Contador's own foundation before turning pro.As a rookie professional in 2017, Mas also helped Contador win his own last stage of the Vuelta, on the Angliru – "and this despite being told by his [then] team not to do that.""I knew he had class and talent," Contador told . "Then every rider evolves as they do, and in the case of Enric it was really fast; he took second in the 2018 Vuelta. After that, as he failed to complete the job [and win]… you know what this sport is like. It seems like if you don't win, nothing is worth anything, and that's why, by winning this Vuelta, cycling is doing right by Enric Mas."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Final lap of Vuelta a España's closing stage in Granada to be neutralised after safety concerns raised
item.author: Dan Challis
item.content:encoded: Following talks between the Vuelta a España organisers and the CPA, the union representing the riders, the final lap of the concluding Granada circuit on stage 21 will be neutralised.Times for the general classification will be taken after the fourth of five passages of the finish line. There will be a stage winner declared after the final lap.In a statement, organisers Unipublic said: “The organiser in agreement with the UCI Commissaires’ Panel have decided to neutralise the time for the general individual classification in Stage 21 starting with the last local lap at 9.8KM before the finish.” “The bonus seconds at the finish will not be counted. The points for the general points classification will continue to be awarded at the finish.”The move comes after concerns were raised about the safety of the course around Granada. The route is littered with narrow, winding roads and dry conditions have made the tarmac slippery in places. Belgian rider Sander de Pestel, riding for Decathlon-CMA CGM in support of third-place Felix Gall, was outspoken in his concerns about the final circuit on Saturday, saying: “It’s not a circus.”“I would not want Mas to lose the Vuelta because of a crash and then have no chance of coming back,” De Pestel told . “And I would not want Roglič to lose another place because of a puncture.”“There are a lot of hairpins on the descents and the roads are extremely slippery through the centre,” De Pestel added. “If someone crashes or has a puncture with 40 kilometres to go, it is impossible to come back,” De Pestel said. “It is a difficult and dangerous circuit through the centre of Granada.”Reports from Spanish newspaper suggested that the Vuelta organisers and the UCI commissaires were initially opposed to any neutralisation, but several teams were insistent that the general classification times should be taken ahead of the finish line in order to make the racing safer. The ruling follows a trend of Grand Tour stage neutralisations in recent years. The new course around Montmartre, which has closed the Tour de France in the last two years, has also been neutralised. Stage 15 at the 2026 Giro d’Italia around Milan was also raced without GC times taken at the end. The undulating final stage in Granada is expected to favour the likes of Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan (both Visma-Lease a Bike), as Enric Mas (Movistar) looks set to become Spain’s first man to win La Vuelta in 14 years. item.title: ‘I just missed 10 metres’ - Oscar Onley drops out of Vuelta a España top five after faltering on final mountain stage
item.author: Dan Challis
item.content:encoded: The final and most difficult mountain stage of the 2026 Vuelta a España was a step too far for Oscar Onley as the Netcompany-Ineos rider faded out of the top five in the general classification.The Scot was dropped on the first ascent of the Puerto de El Purche on Saturday, losing contact with the small group of favourites with just over 90km still to race. A daring attack from Visma-Lease a Bike’s Sepp Kuss vaulted the American from 11th to 5th in the overall standings, bumping Onley into sixth place. Onley did, however, secure the white jersey as best young rider, beating Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) by a few seconds after the final climb to Collado de Alguacil.Hopes were high for Onley’s Vuelta general classification chances after he went toe-to-toe with red jersey Enric Mas (Movistar) on stage 9. However, the 23-year-old has been hampered ever since crashing on a roundabout during stage 12. After stage 20, Onley described a challenging day in which more than 50 riders formed the early breakaway. Following accelerations on the first of four major climbs, Onley just lost contact with the group containing Mas and the other favourites."It was hard. Obviously the way this race is going, everyone wants to go in the breakaway, and the GC group is smaller than the front of the race for most of the day,” Onley said. “Everyone expected [Richard] Carapaz to go. Sepp [Kuss] went first, and Carapaz jumped across. I followed the others, but I just missed ten metres on top of Monachil, the first time, and then the gap just exploded out by the time I waited for the group behind. That was it, really.”Onley paid tribute to his teammates who had supported him, with most of his colleagues making it into the early moves. Once it was clear that Onley did not have the legs to go with the red jersey, the focus shifted to winning white. Should he hold onto the jersey, Onley will become just the second Scottish rider to win a distinctive Grand Tour jersey in history, after Robert Millar’s success in the 1980s.“We focused on protecting the white jersey. We had a really strong team again today. We had most of the guys up the road, so we could connect with them at different points. They really pulled hard.” “I thank them, not just for today, but for the whole race. They’ve been really incredible. The support they’ve given me deep into the stages has been something incredible."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Knicks sign Milicic to Exhibit 10 contract. No, not that Milicic
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: As we near training camp and the preseason, the New York Knicks are starting to fill out their roster, with more than several slots and opportunities still available behind the defending NBA champions’ established rotation.On Saturday, a familiar name entered the Knicks realm when, out of the blue, we read the name “Milicic” linked to the New York franchise.Only, you know, not Milicic.Polish outlet Interia Sport’s Karol Wasiek reported that free agent forward Igor Milicic Jr., no relation to Serbian native Darko, agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the Knicks, allowing the 24-year-old to compete for a roster spot or a two-way deal during the upcoming camp.“@SportINTERIA has established that Igor Milicić Jr. is the next Pole with an NBA contract. According to our information, the basketball player has signed an exhibit-10 type contract with the New York Knicks.” — Karol WasiekThe 6-foot-10, 225-pound forward went undrafted in 2025 following a four-year college career that included stops at Virginia (16 games), Charlotte (66) and Tennessee (37). Milicic averaged 9.4 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists across 37 starts during his final college season with the Volunteers.That said, Igor’s best amateur season came a year earlier when he put up a 13-8-2 stat line shooting 48.7% from the field and 37.6% from three with the 49ers.Milicic spent last season with the Delaware Blue Coats, the Philadelphia 76ers’ G League affiliate. He averaged 6.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 0.9 assists in 18.8 minutes across 45 appearances.The Polish lad also played seven Summer League games with the San Antonio Spurs this offseason, and the truth is that his age, size, and positional flexibility should give him an opportunity to compete for a place within New York’s organization, whether that’s in the majors (more than unlikely) or the minors (slightly less likely).The Knicks currently have all three two-way contract slots available. According to Wasiek, all those openings factored heavily into Milicic’s decision to join New York, hoping to snatch one of them along with the developmental opportunity the Knicks offered him.For context, an Exhibit 10 contract can be converted into a two-way deal, and Milicic could also receive a bonus of up to approximately $91,000 if New York waives him before the regular season and he subsequently spends at least 60 days with the Westchester Knicks.

item.title: 'We always had in mind that Primož lost ten days' – Red Bull satisfied with second overall for Roglič at Vuelta a España despite inability to launch final attack on queen stage
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Despite Primož Roglič being unable to mount a final challenge against Enric Mas (Movistar) on stage 20 of the Vuelta a España, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe were still left satisfied with the performance that should see him finish second overall in Granada on Sunday evening. Roglič started the penultimate day of the race with 1:37 to make up if he was to snatch the red jersey, and even though the German team set things up well with satellite riders up the road in various breakaways, come the final climb to Collado del Alguacil, the Slovenian was forced into defence, not attack. Finn Fisher-Black did the final effort to set him up, but Movistar re-took control with Pablo Castrillo once no move came. It was third-place Felix Gall (Decathlon-CMA CGM) who actually had the strength to launch a move, distancing Roglič, as he and Mas gained more time, but not enough to overtake him for second. "We waited until the last climb and had Finn Fisher-Black to launch him, but then if you don't have the legs anymore to accelerate, then it is what it is," said Red Bull sports director Sven Vanthourenhout to reporters at the finish. "And then, in the end, you have to be happy with second place at this moment."We had three key points. Two of them were really special to do something with Primož. In the end, if he doesn't do the acceleration we talked about before, then you just know that he didn't have the legs, and each performance in the last week was actually a good one. "I think we took everything out of the team and of Primož during this Grand Tour. Then it is what it is, and then it's Mas who is the deserved winner of this Vuelta. I think we can look back on a nice race."Roglič wasn't even supposed to be mounting a serious bid for GC after he was struck by a driver in training at the end of July. However, he's managed to find an elite level despite the lack of training, and land the ninth Grand Tour podium of his illustrious career – should he finish the Granada finale safely. It's been a caveat that Red Bull have long known could see him unable to challenge Mas for red, but they nonetheless still believed in their leader once Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) crashed on stage 8 and blew the GC race wide open. "Of course, we started the Vuelta with Tadej Pogačar, so then already it's always different. And from the moment Tadej was out, of course, we knew that the race restarts again," said Vanthourenhout. "There were other opportunities on the road towards Granada, but we always had in mind that Primož lost ten days before the Vuelta, and that's why we were always careful, and we were always waiting for the last week to take initiative or to do something. "We always had in mind to trust the process towards the end of the Vuelta. [And today], we did actually everything perfect. But, yes, we always should sign for a second place on GC before the Vuelta because we knew what kind of preparation Primož had towards this Grand Tour, and we're happy with it."Looking back to key days where Roglič could have taken more time back on Mas – the stage 18 time trial and Friday's summit finish to Peñas Blancas where he attacked – Vanthourenhout had no regrets."I think we analysed a lot of performance, especially from Primož, and we saw that he did one of his best time-trials ever, and that means that we speak about his best three, four TTs ever," added the Belgian. "So then you have to look back and say this was a good day for us as a team. Then you had [Friday], which was a good one, because we never had the idea to try and gain time towards Enric Mas. We were there as a team. This is what we wanted. This is also what we wanted on Saturday, of course."In the end, Roglič just had to concede to the stronger rider in Mas, who will make history as the first male Spanish winner of the Vuelta for 14 years. Both will be presented on the final podium, as the latest chapter of their rivalry in Spain has finally gone in favour of the home hope.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: The impact Madrid's "six kilometres long" pitlane will have on Spanish GP strategy
Urška Žigart refractures her jaw in crash at Faun Tour Femmes
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Urška Žigart has refractured her jaw in a crash on stage 3 of the Faun Tour Femmes.More bad luck befell Žigart in France on Saturday when she crashed out of third overall during stage 3 in Tournon-sur-Rhône.Žigart's AG Insurance-Soudal team announced the unfortunate news on Saturday evening, stating that her season is likely over as a result of the new injury."Following her crash during Stage 3 of the Faun Tour de l’Ardèche, further medical examinations have revealed a new fracture of the jaw," the team announced."Given the nature of the injury and the fact that it concerns a repeated fracture, Urška’s 2026 season is likely to come to an early end. This would also mean she will miss the upcoming World Championships."Žigart, who finished sixth at the Vuelta España Femenina in May, avoided surgery in June, saying that "all parts of the fracture aligned", letting her start her recovery and comeback quickly. AG Insurance-Soudal said they will monitor Žigart's healing before making a decision on the remainder of her 2026 season, though it seems more likely that she'll return to racing in 2027."Her focus will now fully shift towards her recovery. The team will closely monitor the healing process before making a definitive decision on the remainder of her season," the team stated."We wish Urška a smooth recovery and look forward to seeing her back with the team."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: UCI Gravel World Series: Romy Kasper and Tobias Mørch Kongstad win elite races at Falling Leaves in Finland
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: Romy Kasper and Tobias Mørch Kongstad won Falling Leaves on Saturday, a UCI Gravel World Series race which will next year host the UEC European Championships across two days of racing on Saturday July 31 and Sunday August 1.Kasper (PAS Racing) won a tight elite women's race after fending off Tiffany Cromwell (Canyon-SRAM) in the finale, beating the Australian by four seconds. Local rider Elisa Serné finished in third place."I really enjoyed it. It's a super nice course - a bit of everything," Kasper said afterwards.In the men's race, Kongstad topped a PAS Racing 1-2 ahead of Rasmus Bøgh Wallin after a long solo breakaway. Estonian Riko Tammepuu (UN Cycling Team) was third."It was a long day out there," Kongstad said. "The tactic today was to be in the front. Sometimes it plays out in the correct way and today I was lucky."The 175km finish race takes riders through the Salpausselkä UNESCO Geopark. After leaving from Pajulahti the first 50km takes place on wider scenic roads and through forested sections, then it is onto what organisers describe as a "rollercoaster" with no long climbs but also no flat to be seen. After that is the 35km northern loop, with a mix of dual track rods and hardpack gravel deep in the forests. At Vuolenkoski the race then heads south to return to the Pajulahti start/finish line of the course which is 87% gravel.The race was one of the late season qualifiers for the UCI Gravel World Championships, which is being held in Nannup, Western Australia on October 10 and 11. item.title: USA Cycling Gravel National Championships: Trek Driftless teammates Paige Onweller, Cobe Freeburn secure elite titles
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: Trek Driftless teammates Paige Onweller and Cobe Freeburn secured elite women's and men's titles at the USA Cycling Gravel National Championships on Saturday in La Crescent, Minnesota.Onweller won the elite women's race by just two seconds ahead of runner-up Sarah Lange and 5:29 ahead of third-placed Emma Langley (Ventum-DT Swiss-Kenda-Rule28-Monolith).The 37-year-old attacked solo during some of the course's early climbs before being joined by Lange. The duo worked well together to build a lead before Onweller bested Lange in the sprint."I got her at the end but she really pushed me today," Onweller said afterwards. "Super proud to win."Freeburn secured the elite men's title after crossing the finish line 20 seconds ahead of runner-up Cole Davis (SpeedStudio p/b Basso) and 21 seconds ahead of third-placed Griffin Easter (OpiCure Gravel p/b Orbea and Castelli SOG).The men's race was an active and attritional one. Easter went clear in the closing stages before being caught by the elite chasing group. Freeburn then put in the decisive attack and stayed solo until the end. "The day was great. It was very chaotic, lots of people up the road all the time," Freeburn said. "I've never even been on the national podium before. So, really special to win. I've been thinking about this since last and I really wanted it."Paige Onweller (USA) Trek DriftlessEmma Langley (USA) Ventum / DT Swiss / Kenda / Rule28 / MonolithStella Hobbs (USA) MAAP, ENVE, item.title: One day after comeback stage win at Vuelta a España, Eddie Dunbar crashes out with fractured collarbone
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: After the medical comunicado revealed that Dunbar had come down on his left side after 175km, his team later confirmed he had fractured his collarbone, which will now require surgery. He had been part of the more than 50-rider first chase group behind the breakaway, which was scattered along the road as a brutal, epic queen stage played out. He was last seen being caught by the peloton, but came down 11km from the finish, on the tricky roads heading towards the foot of the final climb, Collado del Alguacil.It's the latest in a long list of injuries for the Irishman, who finally rediscovered his best on stage 19 after a long road back, having broken his ankle in a collision back in March. He's suffered broken collarbones in the early part of his career, broke his hand in consecutive years in 2023 and 2024, and struggled with a knee problem. "Unfortunately, Eddie Dunbar sustained a collarbone fracture on the left side during Stage 20 of La Vuelta a España, so he had to withdraw from the race and will undergo surgery," read a statement from the Swiss team."Eddie claimed victory on Stage 19 of La Vuelta, delivering Pinarello Q36.5 Pro Cycling Team’s first-ever Grand Tour stage win. The team wishes him a speedy recovery."He had been hoping to close out his season at some of the Italian Autumn Classics, but those plans will likely be cancelled as a result of his recovery. item.title: Knicks face tough Miles McBride decision after latest contract-talks update
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: Miles “Deuce” McBride enters the 2026-27 season as the longest-tenured New York Knicks player following Mitchell Robinson’s exit and he’s surely turned into an important contributor for the reigning champs after averaging a career-high 12.0 points while shooting 41.3% from three last season.According to SNY’s Ian Begley, the Knicks and McBride’s representatives have remained in regular contact, but New York’s financial situation could make a long-term extension difficult.“This one is tricky because Miles McBride has definitely earned a raise,” Begley reported. “He’s outplayed his contract (3 years, $13 million) by a significant amount.”McBride is entering the final season of that contract. Begley noted Knicks owner James Dolan’s mandate not to exceed the NBA’s $221 million second apron this season as the major roadblock for reaching such an agreement.Potential extensions for Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart and eventually Jalen Brunson will inevitably increase the money committed to New York’s starting lineup, and McBride looks like the one set to absorb most of the collateral damage — assuming all parties find a way for him to stay.“So there isn’t much financial wiggle room for a McBride extension,” Begley reported.In a promising updated and despite the constraints, neither side has given up on the possibility of extending their relationship.“In a perfect world, those conversations would produce a multi-year extension for McBride,” Begley reported. “The longest-tenured Knick, McBride loves New York, loves his teammates; he was an integral part of this team’s rise.”We all know the alternative, as harsh and hard to stomach it might be: trading Deuce before next year’s deadline. That said, there’s no doubt McBride is one of (if not the absolute best) the lague’s most valuable sixth-man trade chips and would attract significant interest from other teams.“We’re certainly not there yet,” Begley reported. “But logic tells you that’s where things could be headed.”For now, McBride is set to enter the season with New York with one year left on his deal and a date we’ll all remember no matter what ends up happening circled in his calendar: ring night in late-October.

item.title: Record Watch: Five Knicks benchmarks in jeopardy this season
item.author: John Gove
item.content:encoded: Defending a championship changes the vibe during regular-season play. When the goal is to repeat a championship in June, Tuesday night games in February can feel like a formality. Nobody wants to overexert a key player in a meaningless game on the off chance that he’ll blow a hammy. However, Mike Brown’s offense, built for another deep playoff run, can’t help but generate eye-popping stats all season long.Between the exploding scoreboards, higher possession counts, and New York’s elite playmakers and scorers, several Knicks records are suddenly at risk. Some of these benchmarks have survived nearly 40 years, while the ink for others is still wet in the books. A closer look at the roster and statistics suggests five specific franchise records could realistically fall this season. Let’s dive in.Single-Season 30-Point GamesCurrent Record: 36 games – Richie Guerin (1961-1962), Patrick Ewing (1989-90), Jalen Brunson (2023-24)2026-27 Season Target: 37 gamesThe current franchise mark for the most 30-point contest in a regular season is a three-way tie spanning three distinct eras of Knicks basketball. Richie Guerin established the benchmark during the fast-break pace of the early 1960s. Patrick Ewing matched it during his prime, dominating the post game-in and game-out while carrying the team on his broad shoulders and aching knees. Captain Jalen Brunson joined the two Hall of Famers two seasons ago during his rise to All-NBA status.Of every record on this list, this one is the most wobbly. Brunson remains the undisputed engine of New York’s half-court offense, combining incredible footwork with elite basketball smarts.In Mike Brown’s five-out system, defenses can no longer load up in the paint without leaving deadly perimeter shooters uncovered. Having Karl-Anthony Towns at center pulls defensive anchors 25 feet away from the basket, giving Brunson wider driving lanes, fewer double-teams, and access to his mid-range spots. Assuming he’ll be healthy all season (knock on wood and cross yourself), Brunson claiming sole possession of this record with 37-plus 30-point games feels more like a matter of when, not if.Single-Game Scoring RecordCurrent Record: 62 points – Carmelo Anthony (January 24, 2014 vs. Charlotte Bobcats)2026-27 Season Target: 63 pointsFirst, a moment of silence for the Charlotte Bobcats. . . . Okay, we’re good to go.Carmelo Anthony’s 62-point masterclass against Charlotte has stood untouched for 13 years. In a legendary isolation clinic, Melo shot 23-of-35 from the floor without recording a single assist or turnover. Surpassing a single-game point total like that requires the blend of crazy shot volume, incredible efficiency, (no small degree of selfishness,) and a game that’s competitive enough to keep starters on the floor late into the fourth quarter.New York’s current roster is different because it features distinct creators who can completely go off in a single game. Brunson already came within a single point of the record, dropping 61 points on 47 shot attempts against the Spurs in March 2024. Meanwhile, Towns brings a personal career-high of 62 points from his time in Minnesota, with an outside stroke that can cause box score chaos. If Towns hits six or seven early threes while dominating the glass, or if Brunson takes over a high-paced track meet, Carmelo’s iconic record could melt like a stick of butter on a sunny afternoon.Single Season Team 3-PointersCurrent Record: 1,168 made three-pointers (2025-26)2026-27 Season Target: 1,169 made three-pointersNew York set a new record last season, draining 1,168 three-pointers. And Mike Brown’s Knicks are just getting started.Brown’s scheme relies heavily on five-out principles that are designed to distort perimeter coverage. With movement shooters on the bench (Shamet, McBride, and occasionally Alvarado and Clarkson), the sheer volume of perimeter attempts is bound to increase. Averaging roughly 14 made threes a game across a full schedule, and thereby breaking their own team record for a second straight season, seems like the natural trajectory for this squad.Individual Single Season 3-PointersCurrent Record: 283 made three-pointers – Donte DiVincenzo (2023-24 season)2026-27 Season Target: 284 made three-pointersWhen Donte DiVincenzo poured in 283 three-pointers during his lone full season with the Knicks, he shattered Evan Fournier’s previous mark of 241, setting an incredible bar for perimeter volume. Reaching that total requires a player to average roughly 3.5 made threes per game while appearing in almost every matchup.DiVincenzo and Fournier are long gone, but the team has redistributed the heavy perimeter workload across its primary offensive tools. Both Towns and Brunson shoot near 40% from beyond the arc and often get the green light in Brown’s system. If KAT maintains a high-volume, trailing-center role in transition, or if Cap takes even more off-dribble pull-up jumpers, DiVo’s record could easily be squashed before the season’s end.Single Season Point TotalCurrent Record: 2,347 points – Patrick Ewing (1989-90 season)2026-27 Season Target: 2,348 pointsEwing’s 1989-90 campaign remains the ultimate test of single-season scoring in franchise history. Piling up 2,347 total points, Ewing averaged 28.6 points per contest and played all 82 games. Obviously, the big fella served as the team’s primary generator and carried most of the load that year.Surpassing Ewing’s record is hands-down the most grueling challenge on this list of beatable benchmarks. Per-game averages mean little if a player misses games due to load management or minor injury, so any absence from the floor will interrupt the scoring pace needed to top Patrick. Across 77 appearances in 2023-24, Brunson recorded 2,212 points, which put him within spitting distance of the record. To beat out Ewing, Jalen would need to maintain a scoring average north of 28 points per game, while playing in at least 80 contests. Requiring a combination of elite offensive production and availability, the 2,348 points in a season is the hardest to crack, and as Jalen enters his thirties, Coach Brown is likely to play Jalen for shorter stints in unimportant games, to preserve him for the offseason. Still, it is mathematically within reach.Some franchise records are so incredible that they’re unlikely to be toppled, given the changes in play-style, rules, and rosters over time. However, Mike Brown’s team, based on a high-volume, high-efficiency attack, is not your father’s Knicks. In the 1995-96 season, the ‘Bockers averaged 97.2 points per game and attempted 1,285 three-pointers; thirty years later, they averaged 116.5 PPG and took 3,133 threes. And that’s not even top-five in the league! (The Warriors tried 3,616.) With the firepower currently employed at MSG, some of these historical benchmarks are truly at risk.Which records do you think will fall this year? Talk about it below!

item.title: Knicks’ interest in veteran free-agent center emerges ahead of training camp
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks have Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond positioned atop their center depth chart, but the defending champions remain without a traditional third center as training camp approaches and this saga doesn’t feel any closer to an end.In yet another update on the situation, according to SNY’s Ian Begley, veteran free agent Tony Bradley has emerged on the Knicks’ radar as New York continues evaluating potential additions for its remaining roster spots, with a competition for those expected to take place throughout camp and the preseason.“One other note on free agent signings ahead of training camp: veteran center Tony Bradley has also been a player on the Knicks’ radar,” Begley reported.If you’re like me, you probably though Bradley was 35 already. Turns out he’s only 28!Even then, and while Bradley would provide an experienced third option behind Towns and Drummond, don’t expect TB (or whoever ends up landing in New York) to find a clear and open path into coach Mike Brown’s established rotation.Begley noted that the Knicks are comfortable with their current top two options despite the absence of another traditional center, making it even tougher for Mystery Man to get any potential playing time.“The Knicks do not currently have a third center, but there is a strong degree of confidence internally in the Karl-Anthony Towns-Andre Drummond duo at the position,” Begley reported.Bradley spent last season with the Indiana Pacers and Atlanta Hawks, appearing in 41 games and averaging 4.0 points and 2.8 rebounds in 11 minutes per game.The 6-foot-10 center has eight seasons of NBA experience after entering the league as the No. 28 overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. Bradley owns career averages of 4.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 234 regular-season appearances.Begley previously reported that New York has also shown interest in free agents Drew Eubanks and John Konchar while evaluating its remaining roster openings, hinting at the openness of the Knicks’ brass to land a variety of player types ahead of their title defense.For now, the Knicks’ next step is opening training camp before they face the Philadelphia 76ers in the first game of the preseason.

But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and, given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. item.title: Thursday Posted & Toasted Notes: Underdog Knicks, turning point, forgotten Rose
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: Today’s post doesn’t merit an introduction. Just scroll down to the bottom, and you’ll find all you need.Jalen Brunson publicly pushed back on a rumor that he, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges had reunited with former Villanova teammate Matt Kennedy by becoming clients of his wealth management practice.Miles McBride revealed when the Knicks realized they were championship material. He also praised former coach Tom Thibodeau for laying the groundwork, saying, “Thibs did a great job; he built a great foundation.”Mikal Bridges credited the Knicks’ postseason experience for fueling their remarkable comebacks throughout the title run.Josh Hart says the defending champion Knicks are embracing an underdog mentality (how surprising!) despite winning the NBA title.“I don’t think we have a big target. Because I don’t think anyone is picking us to win again. We’re using it as fuel. We’re still the hunters. We’re not satisfied with one. So we’re the hunters, and we like playing that game.”Derrick Rose says he never stopped believing the Knicks would win the championship. “I kind of had them winning the entire time,” Rose said. He also reflected on his own legacy, acknowledging he believes future generations may eventually forget him.Another former Knickerbocker, Danilo Gallinari, reflected on the biggest “what-if” of his career, saying injuries—not talent—kept him from reaching his full potential after being traded from New York in the Carmelo Anthony deal.Anthony Edwards again singled out Madison Square Garden as one of the NBA’s toughest road environments. Asked about his favorite arenas, Edwards listed MSG alongside TD Garden.Kenny Smith believes the NBA was justified in coming down hard on the Clippers over their salary-cap investigation, saying they were “vehemently cheating” and circumventing the cap.EuroLeague owners will hold a potentially historic meeting on Oct. 5 in Lake Como that could determine the future of European basketball, with club owners expected to discuss a possible NBA proposal to acquire EuroLeague following the league’s Board of Governors meeting. Yes, as we all knew from the get-go, the NBA doesn’t just want to expand to Europe—it wants to eat it whole.

item.title: NBA champion Dillon Jones signs camp deal with Philadelphia
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: The Knicks still have no idea what they’re doing with their open two-way spots, but at least for now, one of them will not be Dillon Jones, who signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the rival Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday.Jones has had quite the NBA career so far. He was briefly a Knick on draft night after being selected No. 25 overall in 2024, but his draft rights were traded immediately to Oklahoma City as part of a complicated night for Leon Rose and company.While he didn’t play much as a rookie, he won a ring as part of the 2024-25 Thunder. Most people coming off their rookie seasons on NBA champions would have some security, but Jones was part of the roster churn that OKC continually does to fit new draft picks on the roster, being salary dumped to Washington before being bought out of his rookie contract.Midway through the 2025-26 season, he inked a two-way deal with the Knicks, where he appeared in seven games and played 39 total minutes before being reduced to street clothes for the entire championship run. While you might think he was the least consequential of the 18, his experience as a champion was something Mike Brown leaned on as the reality grew closer and closer.The 24-year-old will now try to latch on in Philly, which has just one open roster and two-way spot with 20 confirmed players in training camp. He’ll be competing with the likes of Tacko Fall and Jameer Nelson Jr.If he does make the roster in some capacity, he will join Ariel Hukporti in receiving their championship rings on Ring Night on October 20 with the rest of the squad.

item.title: Celebrating Deuce McBride’s career and his 26th birthday
item.author: Kento Kato
item.content:encoded: While much of the post-championship celebrations, the fanfare of the offseason, the roster moves, and their subsequent reactions have died down, one New York Knicks player and his future remain very much in flux. Deuce McBride, coming off a humbling Finals that saw him struggle offensively, has been involved in some trade rumors due to the uncertainty of his extension. But while fans and reporters have pondered potential trades and have lamented his postseason performance, some have forgotten just how good and valuable McBride has been. Gone are the days when every team’s best bench players are just prolific microwave scorers. McBride never has, and likely never will put up the kind of shot volume or record the sort of counting stats that garner traditional Sixth Man of the Year considerations. But the former West Virginia Mountaineer is a true “if you know, you know” ball player. In fact, he’s probably one of the more useful names in gauging an NBA fan’s knowledge of true winning basketball players and the non-star analytical darlings of the league. Yet, he wasn’t always like that. While McBride has become one of the more constant and stable rocks of this Knicks team, it wasn’t even that long ago that he was an afterthought on the bench. Stuck behind franchise star Jalen Brunson and fan favorite Immanuel Quickley, McBride began his career racking up DNPs and spending many a night putting on a Westchester Knicks jersey. Like so many players in the rotation, he strived to be in, though McBride never quit. He didn’t ask for a trade. He didn’t pout. Instead, he just worked tirelessly on his game. And the biggest example of just how far he’s come can be seen in his jump shot. While it was notably a major weakness of his early on in his career, the high release, high-arcing shot has now become a signature skill of his.Some of the credit also belongs to the front office. McBride put in the work, but the front office didn’t just stumble into the now backup guard by accident. They drafted him, believed in his development, and his presence was reportedly one of the reasons the Knicks felt comfortable parting ways with the aforementioned Quickley. It’s true that Quickley’s impending free agency and the Knicks’ reluctance to pay him were a big factor. As was the fact that the front office viewed OG Anunoby as the quintessential role player to put next to Brunson. But New York had the utmost confidence that they had a capable bench guard in McBride to fill in after Quickley’s departure. And that’s exactly what he did. Now, he isn’t the playmaker or scorer Quickley is. There’s a chance that McBride never gets there. But his much improved catch-and-shoot ability combined with his elite point-of-attack defense quickly turned him into an irreplaceable piece of the Knicks’ puzzle. He, much like Anunoby but in a much smaller package, was the kind of defender and shooter that could play with anyone in any system. A kin to the reserve guard he replaced, the fans quickly grew to adore him, resulting in the now-famous Deuuuuce chant that can be heard even in road arenas. What made McBride an anomaly, though, was the almost unthinkably team-friendly deal he was on. As the rest of the league and its analysts caught on, he became a mainstay on numerous lists. McBride’s name would show up on the most valuable contracts in the league and best bench players in the league list, amongst others, all while continuing to improve. He was starting some games, closing a lot of games, and regardless of where and when he played, the results were often positive. Very positive. So much that it became hard to find a Knicks lineup with a good net rating that didn’t have his name on it. McBride has had an interesting last couple of years, though. He was rumored to be one of the most vocal supporters of moving on from Tom Thibodeau- a very controversial decision at the time-although that hasn’t been fully confirmed. And he’s been relatively injury-prone during that time. Then there’s the aforementioned Finals performance where his shot had left him and his dribbling, or lack thereof, was put on full display against an incredibly physical and aggressive Spurs perimeter defense. Evaluating McBride on that series alone, and not the multiple seasons of excellent play, is unfair, especially when factoring in the injury he recently revealed he was still dealing with in that series. But all of that has put him and, quite frankly, the Knicks, in an interesting dilemma. The Knicks are clearly better with McBride on their roster than without him. And as of now, he remains one of the most impactful bench players in the league, who also happens to be on one of the best contracts in the league. Barring an unexpected extension, he’s going to hit free agency where the Knicks will likely lose him for nothing. But if New York’s priorities are to win another championship, they should risk that and ride out the year with him regardless of how flawed his offense can look against the elite defenses. But there’s also a possibility they try to prioritize finding another center mid-season by shipping out the backup guard. Regardless of what ends up happening though, it’ll be nice to start the season with McBride. And a fully healthy version of him at that. He’s a damn good player, and he’s now the longest-tenured Knick with Mitchell Robinson up north in Boston. It may very well be his last season in New York, so cherish it and celebrate just how far he’s come. Here’s to Deuce McBride. Happy 26th birthday, champ!
